The text is so small, I have to adjust my screen font every time I use Duolingo, and then change it back to normal after (otherwise all the other apps are grandpa style big). It hurts my eyes looking at tiny text like that. I've reported it but no response yet

DO NOT USE THE MUSIC LESSONS! Their timing and key detection is terrible!! Did anyone even test them?? App is buggy, with the talk exercises turning themselves off, keyboard automatically changing to another language and layout, and exercises submitting while you are still typing. It has so many ads, so what should be a 15mins experience turns into half an hour or more. Do not do any music lessons with a headset, it makes the tempo be half a beat off at random on top of everything else.

I used to love Duolingo. One used to be able to actually learn on the free version with enough focus and determination. In the last two years, they've made inhibative changes that make the free version downright frustrating to use. They no longer have grammar helps available on questions; they've taken away explaining mistakes and moved THAT to DuoMax. They've taken away the option to practice now, and replaced it with an option to watch ads for more hearts. Will the "upgrades" never end?

I am increasingly disappointed with Duolingo. It used to provide a clear series of lessons and encouraged me to practice my learnt vocabulary to recover lost hearts. This is no longer available. The inability to practice to recover lost hearts is motivating me to stop learning languages. I have tried the music lessons and I find the virtual keyboard lags and misses touches on my phone making it too difficult to get the one star to progress in the music playing lesson.

I love everything about this, even though sometimes it feels that in certain lessons and/or units there are only a handful of different phrases being used. I sometimes just memorize its structure, when translated (which isn't the goal of learning a language). also, i would love to start learning Thai, but haven't found a good enough site just yet. maybe it's possible to add it one day - i for one would love that a lot.

I love this app, but there are a few key features that should be available in the free version that are essential to learning a language - specifically the option to explain incorrect answers. Fair enough to have the AI enabled functions and unlimited hearts locked behind the pay wall, but the premium subscription is way too expensive for me to afford.

This app makes learning another language fun. It's great. Not only is it fun, it is also easy to comprehend. The difficulty level increases slowly and as it does it continuously incorporates words and phrases already learned to refresh the user's memory. Each lesson has several different styles of learning, which prevents that monotonous feeling that other language-learning apps often cause. Give it a try. I think you'll love it, I know I do. Thank you Duolingo.❤️

The app could be more challenging at times. Sometimes you can get your way to the correct answer with elimination while thats not an option in real life. And another example is while pairing, trying to have words from similar categories. When I get words like Monday, Pants, Until, Five and Soccer it becomes too easy to realise. Rather have "Pants, dress, shirt" etc. Ps. Super Duolingo ads are too repetitive and long.

Came back after years, waiting still for Slovak to be added but hasn't happened yet. Duolingo works well motivating you, it's intuitive, so I do recommend that. But I'm shocked after coming back and finding so intensely much advertising which wasn't there before. Especially for their own paid programme. Duolingo, I don't need reminding after every lesson, this is way overdone and to no avail.

App is great to start a new language. However, it is too much gamified. XPs are tilted towards practicing at specified times for a specified period, which is unfair. Besides, they could have added tips for each chapter and full explanation after each answer so that it helps you learn more. The worst part of the app is such a loud beep sound after each answer that it won't let you use the app, even if you have lowered volume with someone sleeping around. Hope, they resolve these issues soon.

Duolingo makes learning new languages so fun and easy! I love the streak system, the friendly competition with friends, and the new conversation practice features powered by AI. Sometimes some lessons feel a little repetitive, but overall it’s the best free language-learning app out there.

at first i really love this app. it's cool i can learn a lot of languages, i can even learn math & music BUT the super/max ads this app gives everytime i finished learning is too much seriously. it's so annoying, give it but don't everytime i finished. okay i know the super thing is cool like we can even do training, but NOT ALL ppl have it..so the ads is definitely too much. better if this ads thing is fixed to less ads, i hope u understand the ppl that don't have this super/max pack.

Very confusing and frustrating. Focuses on spelling proper names, doesn't explain why one word is correct over another in context. Today it randomly expects me to "review" TONS of words it's never taught me. I paid for Super Duolingo, so I can keep trying, but everything is literally a guess now and I'm not LEARNING anything. I can't translate a sentence when I've never heard 90% of the words used in it.

Overall the application is fine. There are some considerations: Today's review section is VERY repetitive, you can fo the same exercises 10 times in a row. The speaking mechanic is one of it's weakness (even with native speakers), and hints are not always synchronized with the unit (meaning suggestions are useless). Grammar is inexistent. On every mayor update your progress is lost if you finished the course. The feedback you give takes months to be applied. The family plan is the best option.

Great app. good at getting you hooked with the double, triple points etc once you've completed a lesson. Only deducted a star as years ago when I used it there were community boards and discussions on each question, so if you got something wrong you can learn why it was wrong. I think removing that was a mistake. still a good app for practice though and learning new words, sentence structures etc even if you won't learn the reasons why the language is constructed the way it is.

Lately this app has been lagging too much and it's becoming a nightmare to even navigate through the lessons. I am constantly updating the app in hope for the best but finally I thought maybe purchasing premium plan for super duolingo would solve it but no it is performing even worse than before. For a premium app to behave like this is completely unacceptable.

a good way to pick up some basic vocabulary, but without knowing the grammar rules, it's hard for me to get to the next level. also they charged me for a full year when i tried to cancel my promo the same day as the charge. didn't make me super happy, but did guarantee I'll keep using it to get the money worth.

I enjoy this app, and it's helped me to learn new languages. Weather it was for travel or just fun. It is completely free unless you want to get premium. I do wish it would give you a heart every time you complete a lesson. It makes it very difficult if you earn a heart and can't get any more as you continue. And I wish they had ways that you could earn hearts other than practicing every time. I do highly suggest this app though.

They have removed the option to practice to earn hearts (as in more tries). Instead you are forced to watch and ad or wait 5 hours (it used to be 4). If you are punished to this extent for making a mistake how does this encourage learning. I feel that eventually this ap won't be free altogether. Already they made a more expensive subscription version as if paying a basic monthly amount wasn't enough...

duolingo is very easy to use and also very enjoyable with the games. the only downside would be the hearts, but that's why super duolingo is extra helpful. if you're trying to learn a language, I would recommend duolingo, or even if you want to do art, or even maths! it does take a long while, but that just makes your learning more thorough

The WORST thing about duolingo is that they do not have an option for "vacation mode." I assume students use this app, and during the exam week, it's definitely difficult to keep up with the streak. First of all, the "streak" method to get us to learn is not effective at all. I find myself just mindlessly doing lessons just to get a streak. It's my exam time, and I have no idea what I have learned on duo recently. Please, duo, come up with a better strategyrather than pestering us all day long

Found the app to be quite useful. However, this last week, the app has stopped allowing you to submit speech when prompted. It submits your answer straight away, not allowing you a chance to speak. This is happening on my families iPhone's as well as Android's. Flagged every time in the app, yet no fix with the recent update. 17/03 - still no change.

The amount of ads is genuinely ridiculous now. Often I have to click/wait through 3 or 4 ads. And now I've seen multiple ads for alcoholic beverages. As someone who chooses to be sober for very good reasons I find the ads extremely offensive. Booze ads are the last thing I want to see in the morning, and for an "educational" platform I was surprised to see that they don't care what the ad content is. God forbid there are underage people or folks who struggle with alcohol abuse using this app.

I've been using this app for a while (my current streak is 400+). I think it's useful but I often learn things that native speakers will never use/speak from Duolingo. The math course is ok but weird as I have to estimate my answer on a line. I'm not a big fan of its music course. It's basically a game and doesn't really teach music effectively. I know how to play two music instruments and I was trying to use the music course with someone who knows nothing about music and it didn't go well.

Overall, this is an excellent app. I've been using the paid version to supplement my Spanish learning for months and will continue to use it. There are two changes I'd like to see: 1. I'd like to be able to download as many lessons as I want for offline learning. 2. I'd like to be able to opt out of leagues but still be able to track my friends' progress. As of now, it's both or neither. Once I see those changes, I will update my review to five stars because overall it's a great app!

Duolingo desperately needs to sort out its word practice feature that only gives beginner words or just replace it with old-fashioned flash cards. The lessons are fine but I'm simply not remembering vocab in the long term. I know this because I do weekly lessons and meet native speakers to practice. I pay a family plan so I'd appreciate it to have all the features in working order. I use Anki too, which is fine, but I'd much rather a smart in-built vocab tool in Duolingo.

I've had this for about 3 months now. I love the style of learning the language. I wish they would do something different for the listening in parts. It feels like you are made to fail because they have words you have not learned yet when they speak and then are asked to pick an option which I'll be honest, I get it wrong 50% of the time. If you don't have the super plan, you'll lose a heart for it.

Very frustrating price changes. Annual plan is advertised everywhere on the web at $59. Now it's called super (unlimited hearts) at almost $100. I spent way too much time trying to find the $59 annual plan to no avail. I much prefer transparency to vague marketing. Seems very sketchy.

I used to really love this app, however, it has progressively got worse. Learning has become too heavily gamified, and grammer is difficult to reiview without paying for a subscription to access templates or practice sessions. The 'hearts' system has also become a pain. If stuck on a difficult section, one has to repeatly alternate between a practice session that has no basis is current learning and the main event. There are better apps for each specific language, that I reccomend people look to

edit: Please bring back the "practice to earn hearts" option! I actually learn something in the process, it's a good review and allows you to not feel as forced to progress or redo lessons for practice. Plus you don't learn anything from ads. The only reason its not a 5 star is because there are missing features on android from iphone. The story formed option I find is so useful for comprehension and is not available on Android. If this changes, I'd be happy to give the app a 5 star.

It is great that you can practice languages for free. However you get what you pay (or not pay) for. It is becoming increasingly frustrating. Hints are often wrong or missing. When you work towards challenges, rewards are repeatedly taken away from you. Eg I read same story twice and nothing! While I do not usually care about the games and points, it is disappointing that you miss out on rewards and acknowledgements for your efforts. CS are non-responsive. Please fix if you expect people to pay!

This app can be pretty fun in the beginning, but after a while, the lessons get very hard. Nothing gets explained to you which means you have to figure everything out for yourself. The stories and adventures are insufferable. Don't waste your money like I did on the premium subscription. I haven't used anything else, but I will be trying out Rosetta Stone soon. It's also extremely competitive if you want to move up in leagues.

Very good app for learning languages online. Love that maths and music learning have been added to the list, making it more fun to use. The presence of ads at times is quite disturbing, but not a big deal. And also, when you're taking a speech test in the German language, it doesn't work and wouldn't record your voice, making it impossible to move forward in the speech test or even do it to begin with. This is quite disappointing because you wouldn't know if your German accent is correct.

It's a good language learning app, but there are some bugs I would like them to fix. First, I got First in the diamond league, and most importantly, it said before I was about to get a first, top 10 qualify for the tournament, got First the next morning, and still in the diamond league. Another thing which, I really don't know if it's a bug or not, but when you go to the music course, it pulls up a woman with an electrical guitar, and just sits there forever...

Be careful of which course you're taking, I'm doing Polish and tbh, it's incredibly boring and monotonous! The exercises are limited to typing and choice, there are no exercises to actually help speak, I'm on section 2, Unit 10 and there has been extremely little to do with introducing yourself, and general conversation! It's hardly interactive enough it's just all round tedious!

Duolingo is a good app if you're looking to learn languages. They teach you the basics and the lessons are pretty easy to follow. Please be warned however that if you're using the free plan, you will most likely drown in their ads. There is an ad after each and every lesson and each ad is in an insufferable robot voice. One thing I will critique outside of this is the robot voices. Its hard to get a proper grasp of the pronunciations of a new language, if the one teaching you to speak is a machi

If you want to use this app for free you will be hit with ads after every lesson and if you make more than 5 mistakes you will not be able get full hearts to do more without spending in-app currency which costs real money. So this is more like a paid app that you can trial. For me in Canada their low Tier paid sub is almost $140/yr, or double that for the higher Tier. The price is almost double if you pay monthly. All to "keep education free" :eyeroll:

I'm really enjoying learning with Duolingo. I did French at school and really wanted to re-learn it as a family member lives in rural France and they don't speak much English in that region. Duolingo makes learning a new language (or brushing up on an old one) fun! I pay for the AI package and talk to Lily a fair amount. I'm already thinking about learning another language or doing math when I've finished French.

This app is amazing! If you want to learn a new language but don't know where to start? Duolingo is the best app in my opinion to learn new languages, I wanted to learn Portuguese to communicate with my friend that lives in Portugal and speaks Portuguese. This app has helped me so much!! It may be hard at first but once you get the hang of it it's really easy!

Duolingo is a great app for learning Mandarin! It's user-friendly and easy to navigate, and the lessons are engaging and interactive. The app offers a variety of activities to help you practice your language skills, such as listening, speaking, reading, and writing. It also provides instant feedback on your progress and offers helpful tips and tricks to help you improve your language skills. With Duolingo, you can learn Mandarin quickly and effectively.

Overall, this is a great app - it makes learning new languages fun, and I'm definitely learning. However, it would be better if the app provided guidance when I get answers wrong. Often, I feel like I'm guessing the answers, rather than learning the rules behind verb conjugation, plural forms, etc.

I don't get excited about the points, and gems, because I have NO idea what they are used for. Even paying for a family membership they nag you to BUY more [something] whenever you run out of time on a quiz. I wish they EXPLAINED what new words are. I have to just guess randomly with my a, un, l', les, etc. I have written down a lot on a cheat sheet but it would be better if they just TOLD me what the word means and masculine, feminine, plural, tense, etc. The GOOD thing is that they use

I love it. It is so helpful. just one small thing: sometimes new words appear for the first time and it's asked to translate... A suggestion, too: please make a page with verbs and grammatical rules, which we can consult when we are in doubt. The stories are so nice and helpful. But they are always the same coming back at all the levels. And they are not related to the program of that moment. So, same stories, same speech speed, same grammar issues at level 5 or 35. That should be fixed. 🙏

I don't know if you guys use AI to practice the weak skills but if you do,its all wrong. I am currently doing Korean and Spanish and I already had a pretty good Spanish but I'm practicing it more now. I had one awful lesson with many mistakes but once I passed it,the next lesson gave me the exercises that I aced from that lesson and marked them as hard words which didn't make sense. Also sometimes I lose marks for spelling and sometimes I don't,it should be consistent throughout lessons.

The slider on the math is terrible. Just because I dont get close enough to their arbitrarily chosen point I fail. In German I can fail a whole speaking point just because I apparently cant say "Humbolt Universität" correct even if all other words are spoken perfectly. Also just noticed I was set halfway back a unit in my German? I had gotten to speaking about colleges. Now I have to redo half of the passport stuff!

I'm no longer able to practice for more than one heart. They also messed with multipliers running out and no more streak freezes from chests. The pop-up ads have become loud, long and intolerable. New exercises have you gambling on what the right answer is, even when there should be multiple possibilities. The free version is no longer what it once was. It's as if they're annoying you to upgrade to the paid version. I have a 3 year streak, yet with the new updates I am no longer a happy user.

With the new update they ruined the learning process completely. It is very unrewarding to complete lessons now. All units are in random order without a certain theme, so if you want to repeat vocabulary, you first have to search for that unit for 10 minutes. The path does nothing to improve our languages, instead it is a chaotic way to demotivate progress. Update 2024: They removed the possibility to practice lessons to earn hearts. It's not free anymore, but a paid app with a free trail.

I am deeply disappointed that Duolingo has removed the option to earn hearts by practicing. This change is unacceptable and counterproductive to the goal of language learning. The ability to practice older material not only helped reinforce my knowledge but also encouraged me to use the app more. With the added incentive of gaining hearts, I felt motivated to engage and learn consistently. Now, I find myself using the app far less because once the hearts are gone, so is my ability to continue

Outstanding app. I've been learning Italian for just over 30 days, and I'm fairly confident with simple sentences. The app keeps on your case (if you enable it to) to keep your streak going. The pronunciation lessons are a bit of a pain as it doesn't pick up what I say, but I've only had one penalty due to that issue. The other gripe is that there's one feature you cannot access without a paid subscription. I understand why, but it's a pain none of the less.

I enjoy using this app, but there are a few problems. It doesn't explain grammar or sentence structure, so you just hope you can pick it up. They have also taken away the ability to win back hearts by doing practice lessons, so you have to pay a high gem price or wait 24hrs to get full hearts again, and the monthly price is too high. If it was £6 or £7 a month, I'd be tempted to subscribe, but not ay £10! The adverts have gotten worse, they are very loud, and I'm beginning to want to leave.

Over the last few months, the app has got worse. Considerably worse. Some of the issues that are making the user experience worse is the insistence of pushing American English, rather than actual English - so if you don't have to translate into American you get it wrong (this has got worse and worse. Constant reorganisation of the courses so you end up repeating lessons as they decide to move them around. Now more features added behind paywalls - including the ability to add more lives.

After using Duolingo for over a year to study German, the experience has been positive overall. The app is user-friendly, motivating with its streak system, and covers fundamental vocabulary and grammar well. Listening and speaking exercises help with pronunciation, and spaced repetition reinforces learning effectively. However, it lacks depth for advanced grammar and can feel repetitive over time. Speech recognition can be hit or miss.

Edit: Be aware that when using the free trial and it shows that the cost will then be £4.99/month £59.99 in total, they actually take £59.99 out of your account and not the £4.99 per month!!! So unhappy to have a huge chunk of money taken that i was not expecting. Only google play can refund, Duo dont deal with it! I am really enjoying it. Though I keep getting an error when I try the speaking exercises and despite trying every suggestion to fix it, I just can't fix it.

The latest update is full of bugs, makes the experience worse, and makes it harder to learn with the hearts system. It has bugged out multiple times, with the keyboard crashing so I had to exit out of a lesson, the app failing to track progress, not being able to start lessons, not being able to change settings etc. There are core lessons that are being blocked now and requiring the paid subscription to access. It's wild that they still advertise themselves as a 'free' language learning app.

The one big mark against it is that they seem to want to get you to pay for the app. One way is you get 5 "hearts" a day, and if you lose one every time you get something wrong. If you run out, you either have to abandon the lesson or recharge, for a cost. But they steal hearts. They give you hints, that are wrong, then take a heart for putting what they suggested! I'm seriously considering deleting the app. it's not helpful.

I loved using this app and half the fun was being able to practice multiple times. Yes I made mistakes but that's what happens when you're learning a new language. So I'd put in more practice to gain hearts to continue with my lessons. NOT anymore though, the Devs have become money grabbers and switched that facility off. Got to pay now to be able to keep going with lots of practice. I think that might be a bad move and turn more people away.

It used to be good and fun, but since the last update, the experience has changed. Unless you pay, or have experience of the language you're learning, you will be unlikely to learn much. You can't complete lessons to restore more than one life anymore. It's therefore very difficult to learn, as one mistake means that you can't learn. On the other side, I've just finished a trial of the paid version and it's so easy. You can make as many mistakes as you want and bluff your way into progress.

Amazing app. If you're not a beginner, you don't have to go through аll the lessons and just learn what you need to. You can practice talking, hearing and writing. It has a few ads with the free version but really they're not everywhere on your screen, neither are they unskippable. Just one very small thing : You can't learn several lenguages at a time. But I think that changes with Super Duolinguo. Overall, A. M. A. Z. I. N. G !

Edit: As time goes on this app is getting worse and worse. There's very little value in the paid plans with features being taken away regularly. No more forums was a massive blow for me as I used them to get insight into grammar rules etc. which Duolingo does a really poor job of teaching. [5* Hands down the best language learning tool out there. The hardest part about learning a new language is being intimidated too early on and Duolingo eases you into it and challenges you as you progress.]

I'm commited to a year of Spanish, but I'm getting annoyed with some of it - mainly its juvenile obsession with sport and schools/universities, which gets stale very quickly. It seems to be teaching Latin American Spanish. Sure, you'll probably be understood in Spain, but there are differences. And you need a brief course in American English to avoid confusion - Americans, most of the world doesn't call football 'soccer' or autumn 'fall'.

Engaging and rewarding in a game-like way. The notifications can be a bit much - quantity and aggression. Some things are oversimplified imo - lack of grammatical explanation, translating tense incorrectly, constant multiple choice instead of typing - but it's still educational. (This is based on my experience in Spanish and Japanese.) I don't like how you automatically follow people when you're "invited" to someone's Premium. You had me following opps. Add Tagalog / Filipino please!!

I was a bit skeptical to use Duolingo again after the whole revamp thing, and after i heard they got ads now. but turns out it's still great, the ads are only after lessons, and right after i finish my super free trial, they immediately offered me another week free??? i don't know if this is a mistake on their part but i'm glad i'm able to learn a new language on a budget.

They recently limited earning hearts by practicing to only one heart, only when you have 0 of them. It makes it extremely hard to use the app and actually learn the language if you don't use the premium. I have used the app for years, and have a 1780 days streak, but this might actually force me to stop using it, and move to another platform or a tutor, instead of paying for a premium. I really hope this is a big that will be fixed soon, and not a feature with a goal of forcing people to pay.

Scam! I used to love the app, Signed up for a auper duo lingo free trial, The app said I would be notified before the trial would end, I chose to only do the trial, because I simply can not afford to keep duolingo. I never received an email or in app notification my trial was about to end, and suddenly waa charged about €100 for a yearly subscription. I don not have the money to pay for this, whoch means I wont be able to pay groceries for the rest of the month now.

I have been using it for a long time (with Duolingo Plus nearly 3 years), but now that I have the opportunity to use my knowledge seems like if I didn't knew anything, all the grammar explanation for small languages is almost forgotten in the app, the only thing that could change this point is a more detailed grammar explanation section, like the one that appears up top every path, besides this huge disadvantage the whole app is good for learning languages. Plus music course is buggy.

Really, Duolingo is that app for learning. I've been privileged to use a lot of learning apps, but Duolingo methods are really among the top tier, and they work. Simple things like streaks and the rewards really keep pushing. And the UI and total experience remains true to the app's policy of fun learning. Also really enjoying the new music and maths!

Duolingo used to be great. I'm on my second language right now, and I almost have a 1000 day streak. But whoever is running the business are a bunch of greedy scumbags. They keep changing the app, to try to force you to pay their ridiculous price for super Duolingo. For example you used to be able to do practice, that would regenerate hearts if you were low, but you can't do that anymore, and they took away my streak freezes fornko reason. I'm considering just stopping at this point... Very sad.

Great app for learning languages. But I hate the hearts stuff. If you make a mistake, you lose a heart, and you learn by making mistakes, and you can onlg make 5 mistakes. So it's basically punishing you for learning. It doesn't give me any motivation to keep on going. Please remove the hearts. It would make the app way better and actually help me learn faster.

I don't see ads because I use ad blocker, but I could imagine the pain if experiencing it after every lesson. I hate that the radio lessons uses a synthetic (AI?) voice now. It no longer feels authentic. How are we going to learn authentic human-made languages if it is based on something artificial? Furthermore, I don't think this app helps a lot in certain languages for a good amount of people. Do search for alternatives just in case.

Reducing my score more due to recent changes to remove certain perks from free users. I was loving the app and am still trying to use it. But taking away the ability to practice without needing hearts means I'm unable to memorise things as well and it's moving too fast. Bring back the ability to practice to earn hearts and i'll give it 5 again as it was really helping with my vocab

This app has gone downhill since I got it two years ago. They lock free features behind a paywall and push AI powered subscriptions onto you. And for an app that "uses ads to fund their teaching," they sure do love not teaching with how many times a right answer wasn't accepted and with giving users random words they haven't even been taught yet. It's good for starting a language and that's it. Don't even try the music lessons unless you want to get pissed.

I understand that this is a free service, and I am grateful for the opportunity to practice. However, I am disappointed that I have lost the chance to practice for free hearts, as I feel this would be beneficial to my learning. Please sort this out. May I add that this application appears to prioritize game-like elements, such as earning experience points and advancing through leagues, rather than genuinely facilitating language learning.

For regular users, Duolingo is a fun distraction that is also educational. It uses a hearts currency to incentivise less mistakes but comes at the cost of ads. If you become a super duolingo member, you no longer have to watch ads, you get infinite lives and unlimited legendary challenges. My only wish, is a word bank that you could look at without trying to match words, that allows you to browse and recall but otherwise Duolingo is top-notch.

Had to delete some of my original review to fit this edit in; speech recognition is poor; "oh damn" does not sound like "Es ist ein Bär" and my German friend got the pronunciation wrong frequently when she tried it. I'm told by native speakers that there are errors. Also it's more useful for speakers of American English as other English speakers will loose lives for translating café as café and kino as cinema. English sentence construction is often odd too. No room to say more

I'm getting very frustrated after working for an hour. I see that NONE of my points earned have accumulated. In fact, they went down. It's happened many times in the past, making me drop down levels week to week. Looks like the double or tripple points calculation is not working - even though it is showing the amount before I watch all those ads. Got to fix this!

1 star for stealing paid features and making a great application worse every day. It was an application that could teach you a language. I am on 998 day streak and learning Spanish for 60-80 minutes a day. And it works. But: 1. When I paid my annual subscription - I had a personalized practice. Now they moved it in new, more expensive plan, stealing it from me. Guys, I paid for it! 2. I also had a practice section. It is stolen too. Just deleted. 3. Nothing to do after finishing the course

Duolingo is going a bit downhill in my opinion. I pay for premium and now I'm constantly bombarded to get the "Max" for another ungodly money! Additionally after each lesson there are way too many click to actually complete it. It feels like it's turning into yet another "just keep your streak" app. Honestly after many years of using this app I'm not really sure it brings enough of value anymore to pay the premium.

Decent app for learning basics of a language. The free version is unusable as they punish you for making mistakes so you can't continue as if the excessive ads weren't enough. And also it doesn't allow you to practice to earn hearts anymore. There also isn't much value in continuing the course after finishing as the daily refresh is always the same so you end up memorizing it all after a few tries. Old lessons only give 5 xp but at least it's a better veriety than the daily refresh.

Great app for learning new languages, but I have seen the difference in effort depending on the course. For example, I would like more types of exercises in my Polish course, like speaking, stories, etc. that others like Spanish get. I just finished my Polish course and I don't think I know enough Polish, PLEASE EXTEND THE COURSE. Glad that they fixed the gross snot icon, but why did they randomly remove the dark mode feature? My app had been in dark mode for a long time, even though I didn't have dark mode enabled overall on my phone. I loved it. Now the app uses light mode even though I didn't change any of my phone settings. I can't enable dark mode overall because it messes up my phone's theme.

1 . Lessons loading too slowly to be useful. 2. Feedback option in application doesn't seem to work => Drop a star After a period of rapid changes and problems tracking learning progress the application seems to settled down. The problem with application memory usage rapidly increasing also seems to have been at least partially resolved. The application still seems to be relatively indeterminate in awarding double XP. Sometimes double XP is awarded but not applied.

The ads have recently become so obtrusive that the app is unusable. After each completed lesson, I must close the app and then reopen in order to progress any further. After completing over a six year streak, it's hard to say goodbye. But, the app is no longer fulfilling what it had promised.

Pretty good for learning a language, breaks it down into manageable chunks. Sometimes it swamps you with new words when you could do with extra practice. The points system is broken. Sometimes says I'm earning triple, but only gives me 1.5x. Other times it says a lesson is worth 30 but only gives me 15. And the speaking element doesn't work properly. There's also an element of woke ideology, meaning it wants you to learn phrases that you won't need unless you're going on a woke holiday.

Okay. Despite all the negative comments let me keep it frank. It is true, I do not recommend using the free version, but the super version is very much worth it. And I am from a country where the currency exchange is bad so its relatively expensive for me. 60 dollars a year if youre serious about learning is really not that bad so I dont get the negative comments. I notice you also get more XP per lesson when you move up to B1 levels so it helps with leaderboard if you care about stuff like that

The app was great at first when I was able to get the free trial subscription. But now that I have to pay or use the free version, I doubt I'll use it as much. If the app was worth paying nearly $100/year, I would but I don't think it's worth it. I get many says that make no sense "the bear didn't play the piano", well duh but who would say that in real life? There isn't enough real life scenarios so how can it be helpful? But hey, at least I can say the bear doesn't play piano in German 🤦‍♀️

this app is a good way to learn a language it startsoff very easy and then helps you progress at your own pace. its very beginner friendly and if you already know a unit it allows you to skip. just saying I've learned more Spanish here than i have theough the public school system. Oneday i would like to see an option for sign language!

I've been in using the Duolingo app for two years now. Although I know I could be further than where I am if I spoke my chosen language more frequently, I enjoy learning at my own pace and seeing the milestones achieved. Duo cannot do this alone, so the other characters make it a more interesting (Lily is my favorite 🥰😂). I look forward to continuing to my learning.

I've been using this app for a couple of years now, and I really enjoy using it. They've added MATH, which used to be my WORST subject as a child. I went back to college at age 28, and I suddenly understood it better. Math is LIFE. It makes you think and analyze. I LOVE that they added this because I'm 45 and need to sharpen my skills. I can also speak some Spanish. I never got past Spanish two in junior high. Now I can small talk. 😍 This app is relaxing, too. I look forward to it daily. ♥️

WORST thing about this app: the INSIPID 15 second ad for Super Duolingo after every. single. lesson. There is also an ad before it that you can skip after 5 seconds. I'd rather have 2 normal ads than the 15s Duolingo ad. I finish a lesson in ~100 seconds, so 20s of ad REALLY slow down my progress. Plus in the unpaid version, you get 5 hearts and if you make 5 mistakes, you're done for the day. Which seems self defeating cause then they can't feed you more ads. all that aside, it's effective

The experience with the app gets worse and worse over the time. Where should I start from? First you increase the "price" of league games. Over the course of 1 year, it went from 10 gems to 30, and then to 100. Now you are removing the option to gain heart with practice. You are basically forcing users to pay, even though they are paying with their time watching the ads. Pathetic!

The recent update is terrible. If it ain't broke don't fix it. This app was an effective resource for learning and now it has been turned into something of a trivialized game. 9/24 Edit: suddenly getting a lot of political messages inserted in my lessons. I just want to learn a language....

Absolutely fantastic app that helps you learn a language. It won't get you to fluency on its own, you have to actually practice and use what you've learned on it, but it's great. I will say I could do away with the creepy weird icons they sometimes change to... I guess they're trying to be quirky? Some of them are just disturbing.

Some languages don't have a good explanation. And when I answered with what I had wrote, it was wrong, even though the word or sentence is the same in English. Why don't Japanese lessons use kanji? Sometimes I get the wrong answer because of it. Kanji is one of the official Japanese writing system and is very important. Also, some questions are lack of context. E.g. ドリンクバー was translated as self-service drink bar. How can I know it was self-service? I just know it's a drink bar as it written.

It's not terrible, it's massively improved since the last time I tried it. I will say that I am a Brit and a lot of the English translations are in American English, it would be nice for British English to be an option because I get confused and answer wrong. Also I'd love to be able to move the 'selecting words' rather than having to get rid of them all and reselect to change the order, but overall, it's a fun way to learn vocab

When experiencing a particularly difficult section (irregular verbs, conjugating root words) more quidance and explanation to better understand would be nice. Since my weak spot is not being able to understand what others are saying, more storys, podcasts etc. would benefit me. Also more variation in voices.

This is one of the best language apps I've ever seen! I'm usually bored after 5 minutes of learning, but this keeps me motivated to keep going. I know it will take a while for me to learn, but I'm committed to keep going. Duo keeps me motivated and I'm not frustrated for making a mistake, I can just try again. And the in app purchases a extremely fair, almost everything is free. And Super duolingo is completely optional. I'm able to get hearts super easy without it. Keep up the good work! 😄

Duolingo is the most ubiquitous language-learning software I know of, and for good reason. For beginners and intermediates, I can't think of a more accessible alternative, and its prominence means there are more than likely friends of mine I'm able to level up alongside. My only gripes are that I wish there were fewer ads for the premium version, more ways to interact with other users, and a greater variety amongst the kinds of challenges possible. Even without those changes made, it's amazing!!

Beginning levels are great for when you want to learn a little of the language of a country you are visiting, but after that I would not use this to learn a language from scratch. I use it everyday but only to supplement the formal classes I'm taking and to keep my vocab up now that I no longer live in the country I was learning the language for. You have to get Max in order to actually understand why you got a question wrong and there's no real explanation of grammar prior to doing a leason.

Lately, when completing daily quests, it's not always rewarding you with appropriate credit toward the monthly quest... it's an insignificant bug but it's annoying. That said, forget some overpriced apps & other services... this is a great free/cheap way to learn languages.

Edit: TEAM DUO FIXED IT!!! :D I was really upset with the new Norwegian update because the exercises stopped working and the voices went weird and wrong sounding but they've fixed it and put the voices back to the proper sounding voices so now I'm really happy!!! ^.^ Thank you for fixing it Duo team!! I can understand what they are saying again now and the course sounds like my other Norwegian resources again instead of completely different/wrong pronunciation. 5* for fixing it! :)

I have been using Duolingo since the COVID shutdowns and have learned a lot. I really have my doubts about its effectiveness as a stand-alone method of learning language but it has been very useful for me. A quality of life improvement that would be easy for them to fix would be to PLEASE move the reward for finishing a friend quest beneath the night owl/early bird rewards since it has better longevity. I can't tell you how many times I accidentally wasted the friend quest reward.

Fun tool for building regular language learning habits, but definitely shouldn't be used as your ONLY language learning resource, since you are going to miss out on a lot of grammar side learning, at least from my experience with the Japanese course. But you do get a lot of repeated exposure to a lot of useful vocabulary so that makes Duolingo a beneficial routine-enhancing habit building tool, mainly for language studies, to be used ALONGSIDE other more in-depth tools and resources! :)

Great app, has helped tremendously. Could use some work with accepting certain answers like "telephono" when its actually spelled "telefono". I would love to be able to give my 2x exp to people as i dont have the time to do 3p minutes of duolingo a day and hate to have them go to waste as you typically earn them after 10-20 minutes of duolingo.

duolingo's a good tool to be used in conjunction with in-person french learning :)) however, with regards to the interface itself, i hope duolingo can roll back its removal of profile pictures. i don't see why users should be forced to create avatars since anonymity is a priority for many. my suggestion is just that profile pictures should be brought back. thanks!

I've never been very good at learning languages but I seem to be getting on with this method used by this app so who knows, perhaps I'll be able to get by in Lisbon. EDIT IN 2024 I'm starting to wonder if Duolingo is really good...at getting you good at Duolingo. Let me put it another way. I don't think that, on its own, it will teach you true understanding of a language, nor how to SPEAK it. It's a good tool, but it can't be the only tool.

It's a good learning app, it helped me learn spanish and other languages a lot, but without super duolingo, it's VERY annoying, after every lesson you finish, there's an AD like they're forcing you to get super duolingo Overall I recommend downloading if you wanna learn a new language (you can also joke around with your friends about duo)

Been having a lot of issues lately with the exercises not being counted once I finish them. I've had to redo exercises 3 or 4 times over. Closing the app and coming back sometimes helps but it will usually just count one exercise if anything. So frustrating to keep doing the same exercises and not progress

The format of Duolingo really helps me learn languages quickly. I enjoy the ability to review any lesson anytime. My only wish is that there was some kind of anime or video that would play a short at the end of each unit using the language and words learned. This would greatly improve the understanding and learning of the spoken language. I would have given a 4.5 if that was an option because of this hole in the learning process. Gave a 5-star review because the app deserves more than a 4.

I absolutely love it 🔥 I love how they fixed the leaderboard bug. I love the new features that have been added especially to the Japanese lessons content because it was only Kanji practice but now there is a mini podcast which makes learning Japanese even thrilling since we don't really have any stories to read like in all the other languages. I do wish the podcasts were a tad longer, but hey, it's better than just practising Kanji. Learning a language has never been this thrilling.

Currently on the free version and wow, my wife and I are learning Japanese. hands down best.. well... duolingo app ever ahaha :D had a demo of the paid version for 3 days, and it was also amazing 👏 really big round of applause to the team that made this and would also like to say thank you, you guys bring people together across languages. respected! :) :)

I was told about dualingo by a friend. So excited to see Hatian Creole! I went to Haiti on a Mission Trip when I was 9 and 11... and wanted to take it in high school... Needless to say, French was the closest. not quite close. I did also sign up for Spanish as I have forgotten it. I am struggling more with the grammar part of it. I felt the Spanish one is a little more organized to understand and implement that. I also got 2 days of the paid. As someone who is low income, that is incentive!

It's a really good tool to help learn languages. Using it for free is a nice and viable option if you keep your A game on. But if your off one day, it really messes up the learning process. They pitch Super often, which fixes alot of the free 'option' problems. So if your serious, it's probably the best option. But as far as I can see they only sell one year subscription at a time? Something that makes it a bit more of a commitment then I'd like. Monthly would be best. Either way. Good app. 😁👍

Great app! I've been learning a new language for more than a year now and it did help me improve, but I experienced some issues about the achievements. I have been collecting more than 200+ words and have collected the 4 of 10 Word Collector for the FIFTH time but it keeps resetting and going back to 3 of 10. I hate that because I'm a sucker for achievements 😅 , hope the problem would be fixed!

It's pretty good overall, but your speaking exercises need work. Firstly these courses will have you repeating the same 2-3 sentences and, secondly, there seems to be an issue with them as sometimes they won't accept the correct answer no matter how many times I say it. It’s clearly a bug. I restarted my device, tried at different times, but nothing worked. It gets stuck on one specific word and prevents me from completing the exercise. After a few "give it one more try" it simply fails you...

I have had Duolingo for over a year now and can honestly say that it is a great way to begin learning a language. The repetition really helps with vocabulary and they make the learning fun, but it is too repetitive and does not provide enough opportunities to spontaneously form sentences of various topics, so you mostly become proficient at transcribing the other language.

This is a great app to learn languages for free. I can learn from the basics-alphabets, simple words, verbs, constructing sentences, pronunciation. There is a feature to review mistakes and perfect them. I also love the blogs. Little fun facts. Recently, I started learning music too, it is super fun. I am a complete beginner, so I find it hard to play piano music with the music in the background. Is that like a metronome?

This used to be an amazing language learning platform, which worked equally well in the app and the browser. Around 2021, however, the browser version felt somewhat left behind. Also, explaining the mistakes and the alternative ways to say something aren't available anymore either. But, the worst thing is the most recent (2025) update with which you can't simply practice. Once you lose your hearts, there's no repair. You just lose your streak. Planning to abandon Duolingo!

Great app. I love that it keeps incorporating "old" content in progressively longer intervals together with introducing the new one so that I don't forget it. I keep practicing all 4 skills: speaking, listening, writing and reading, all at my own time convenience. I can do a lot or a little in a day depending on my time availability. Love it, it works.

A very interesting and beautiful app for learning languages. But, please minimize the number and duration of ads, which is really annoying factor. It would be great, if good features of other Duolingo versions are nicely integrated in an existing version itself. There should be some willingly exit option for those who finish their all lessons along with the tournament and want to learn something new from the app. Kindly make the app more learning-focused rather than competition-based. Thank you.

It started well (see below) but it is such a bug filled app it fails too many times. Now two of my family group have been unable to use the speaking part of the app for weeks! There is no way to address this with the company. They take your money then leave you hanging! former review... Amazing way to learn a language. Intuitive and easy to access. It is the best I have found... I wish this was available 40 years ago!

What a great idea for an app. I have really improved my language skills. I like how the lessons are structured. What I can't stand (especially as a paying customer) is how bugged the app is. Every second day the experience boosts ( which I spent considerable amount of time earning) just disappear or just change from x3 to x1.5 etc. No big deal if it happens once, but it's been ongoing for months now, and customer support basically doesn't exist. Not even for a paying customer

Edit: Since the recent updates, the ads have been causing issues. It freezes on adds to chat with lilly, you complete lesson, and the XP isn't logged. There are lots of glitches. it's such a shame as I absolutely love Duo. After years of private tuition with zero effect I suddenly feel I am making progress with languages. Easy to follow, fun to use and effective.

Terrible. I've been using Duolingo for a couple of years and been progressing quite nicely. All of a sudden, they've changed the syllabus and dumped me in the middle of a course where 60 per cent of the vocabulary and grammatical concepts are unfamiliar. And they don't give you the option of going back to repeat lessons; just grope around by trial and error. Absolutely furious.

Good, but there also other numerous bugs and glitches like one where it set me back an entire unit, and another witch reset my streak even when I had a streak freeze. Pls fix these annoying bugs so people can enjoy the game more. Edit: Also now realize the ads are very annoying sometimes, like I get one ad, then I get another one at the same time. Its very annoying and in your face, because you should only get one ad (which I'm fine with getting) after a lesson. Pls reduce ads at one go. Thx

It's a fun app. I found my level improved with the subscription as it was uninterrupted by ads and trying to get lives. I don't like how sometimes you end up using double time, but there's a problem on the system, so it's wasted. Another thing is how people can send you messages, but if the thread has come off your feed - you can't click on it and add your comments. Furthermore, no one ever responds if you write to the company. It would be helpful if you can restart a course if you've forgotten.

I have been using Duolingo for several months now, and it’s been a great language-learning tool. The app is easy to navigate, engaging, and keeps me motivated with its interactive lessons. I particularly like the way it breaks down language learning into small, manageable sections. The gamified experience with streaks and rewards makes it enjoyable to keep learning every day. It’s also great for all levels, from beginners to more advanced learners.

Just done 3 weeks and I'm quite disappointed. I will continue for a while to see if it gets any better, but I doubt that. The super (paid) version provides very little benefit for actual learning. the biggest difference is the ads. Every 2-3 minutes there are 2 ads in free version and that's way too many. The pro (AI) is a gimmick and just proves that the lessons are not made by proper tutor, but mostly algorithm or random only. Can't use headphones cause ads are way too loud compared to content

Good... But not good enough! Relentless ads, and they are mostly super long. 5 hearts let's you make only 5 mistakes then... yep more ads to try and regain them. Slightly repetitive but sometimes that is good to embed it into your brain. I was very interested in subscribing until I looked into it and you get charged yearly, which is very misleading as it puts a monthly amount on there when opting to purchase. I will use for free until the yearly pay option changes.

It's good for learning a language, but of course it's missing a lot of things. For example, I've been learning French and it practically doesn't explain anything, and just tells you the literal translation of a word, and if you're lucky, the word's gender. You have to figure it out yourself and it's a bit limiting. Also the ads have gotten SO ANNOYING, to the point where EVERY SINGLE LESSON gives me 2 unskippable ads.

I love the app and the variety of games provided to aid learning. However, I have given it 3 stars as the app is just too buggy and has me restarting lessons in order to progress as I often get a red error box when selecting words for some of the exercises. I have tried to submit a report for feedback on this, but I've had no response. This is frustrating as I have paid the premium and would expect a better service. I love learning but don't have the patience to keep restarting lessons.

Duolingo makes language learning fun with its gamified lessons and cute design. It’s great for beginners and helps build daily habits. But if you're aiming for fluency, it’s best as a starting point—not a full solution. Still, for a free app, it’s pretty solid and keeps you coming back with streaks, challenges, and that slightly threatening owl.

Make the app icon static again!!! If i want my main screen changing every now and then, i can use a widget! I've been so happy with duo for years, but most of the recent features just make the app worse. I miss user comments and forum knowledge base, i'm sick of constant structure and reward systems change, and removing grammar tips from the original course creators was a crime against the language learning purpose. It would be a shame to drop a 2400 streak, but i'm close to it as never before.

App is glitched, can't progress to next lesson. The worst part is I should get a chest, but because clicking on the lesson results in an error every time, I'm not gonna get it before the time runs out. Updating didn't fix anything. Reinstalling didn't fix anything. I'm just screwed. I bypassed it by skipping to the next unit, but it happened again in that one. It's always finishing the Kanji Practice that breaks it. So now I have to learn by skipping units and never getting chests.

first, dark mode stopped working for me. tried to contact support for this but was completely ignored. then, although I have animations turned off, new animations popped up with no way of deactivating them. and then, I started getting some real creepy artwork of Duo whenever I finished a lesson. but the worst thing by a mile is they started to automatically send you to the pick a subscription plan screen after every ad. you get an ad after every lesson. it's become very unpleasant using the app.

When I first started using Duolingo, I thought it was great. But over time, I noticed the app's AI system started getting weaker. Many times, it wrongly marks correct answers as incorrect.The same easy-level exercises keep repeating, which makes the learning process boring. What started as a fun learning journey eventually became repetitive and frustrating .It might not be bad for casual learners ,but it is not good option for serious learners in the long run . --- Duolingo Review (Negative)

it's very good app for new learners. I learnt Korean in just two and there are many options if you want to change your course. you can learn music math languages like Korean, Hindi, Tamil, Marathi,Japanese and Chinese. Duolingo motivates you everyday on your home screen this motivated me a lot and now I am very fluent in Korean. if you make a mistake if else is do it again and again but it's not that stressful. so I suggest you download Duolingo. because it's a very nice app.

What used to be a really decent app now focuses on making money, thus, started including lives that you lose when you're marked wrong if you have the free version. Which is highly likely as a lot of answers are very inflexible and often do not accept alternative translations. Reported problems rarely get fixed due to loads of users and not enough staff, even when you email. For example, you get 1/3 exp on the scoreboard from what you get from lessons. Already emailed about it, but no response.

for a free app it can't be beat, instead of playing a game you can play this and learn a new language and of you want to fast track it, the subscriptions is more than reasonable. that was my 5 star, now it's 2 because the app locked up and won't open other than to a solid green screen that says duolingo. deleted it, re-downloaded and now I can't log in, even the online version won't allow log in. Going to lose my streak by no fault of my own.

I've been using Duolingo for about 2 years. It wasn't perfect but I enjoyed using the app. I learned some basic Italian and Japanese. The last updated killed that. The new learning tree is terrible. The lesson are repetitive and dull. The progression is linear to a fault. You can no longer choose which lesson you want to do. Finding old lesson to brush up or practice is impossible because they are only labeled by them. Other might find the new Duo more useful or fun. I certainly don't.

Constant messages and buttons asking you to pay money: to get more XP, to get more gems, to extend the time for match madness to meet the daily quest, and on and on. It feels like a casino, constantly nudging you to pay more. Keep in mind that this is with the paid family plan subscription. Furthermore, on the practice screen you cannot choose the type of practice. For instance I would prefer untimed word match that helps me remeber the words, but no, I cannot have that.

I used to love this app for years. Today, i am frustrated with it. I've updated the app. Constant ads about Super Duolingo, and when i even considered to pay for it, i can't because "something went wrong". There is no dark mode anymore, too light for my eyes, i have to pay for every challenge and i don't have enough xp to pay for it, because i want to learn casually, not frantically, to get xp. Also, with every update, i lose a lot of my progress. I am sorry to say that i might be done with Duo.

Honestly, learning has been fun. It's just the 1.5x 2x, and 3x XP system after completing goals has been error for so many times that even after completing goals and the notification for 1.5x or 2x or 3x XP show up, my XP is still 1x. I know this is for learning, but since I'm a bit competitive, it's a bit irritating if I can't maintain my ranking because the XP system is broken.

the app is really good, I enjoy it. however, I'm doing the Welsh course, and some of the features like the 'speak' section aren't available for it. I also wish there were more explanations about words, mutations, and rules. I spend a lot of time goggling why certain words change after certain letters, etc. it's quite frustrating.

Frustrating app. Very well designed to get under the skin. Recent update shave taken away some of the features that made it a fairer app. Starting a lesson before the time runs out but completing it after the time runs out is no longer counted in the xp or the friend quests...the recent update means I can't do speaking lessons. No matter what I do check permissions reinstall, the speaking lessons don't work. My rating remains unchanged at 3

I've a family account now and it's a great way to pass the time instead of socials. I wish it wouldn't activate XP boosts automatically. I'd like to use them when I have sufficient time and focus instead of just when I look at the app briefly. Improvement: Allow us to drag words. Improvement: Let us to search learned words. Feature: Teach us things like numbers, days, months in a new module instead of randomly as we come across them one at a time.

Uninstalled. The lessons are monotonous and I've just done a week of "I eat cold rice everyday" and all of a sudden my "weak" skills are "the photo is between the window and the table" which doesn't make sense as I haven't learnt object locations yet. The difficulty just randomly spikes with no reason and out of context. The league is exhausting and I don't feel I'm learning anything, but rather tricked into feeling I've learnt something.

Overall the app is fun however I do have quite a few issues with it. I think it's not really explaining the grammar well. you do have some notes but that's not nearly enough and leaves me a little confused. Also the voice exercises are abysmal for me. I have developed a fear for them as it rarely registers my frist word. It also sometimes ends the recording before I even finish saying the sentence.

terrible app. makes you watch a 30 second ad then doesn't give you the reward. AI generated voices sound nothing like human beings so it is impossible to improve your listening skills. Doesn't recognize when you say the simplest words, uhhh i'm pretty sure i'm pronouncing the word "Si" correctly duolingo... I guess its fine if you just use the free version for introductory purposes, but it the anyone who pays for it or expects to actually learn a language with it will be sorely disappointed.

The language learning content is great, but the tech side is a pain. The speaking exercises continually glitch and don't work. My partner and I have had this issue for years (several different phones) - deleting / reinstalling only works until the next update and tech support stopped responding a few reports ago. Its been happening this time for several months. I stay for the language and put up with the glitches, for now.

It is a very helpful and motivates me to keep learning, lots of languages to choose from. Rewarding when you complete lessons. If you want to learn a language, then you should get this app, And it's free too, which is good. The heart system is a little annoying though, but thats about it. 4 Stars. (and there's a bird, so thats cool)

I have a paid subscription, but probably won't renew. The phrases are sometimes just obscure and not useful. I used to enjoy doing the monthly challenge but they just ramp up the learning goals so it became unobtainable so I just switched off. * EDIT * After stopping my sub I get one heart every 5 hours. How are you ever going to progress with that? The app has just turned into a way to squeeze money out of people and so I've uninstalled.

free version is getting so annoying to use. Before, the ads were manageable and not annoying at all, with only ONE short ad. Now I have to watch one ad for an external and then a second stupidly long unskippable ad for super Duolingo. I hope to god this gets fixed, because it's so annoying when I want to get lots of practise in during class and then have to deal with half my time on the app being wasted by ads. I have better stuff to do, please get rid of this.

Came here specifically to write a review after spending a full 60 seconds watching an annoying ad for a freemium game. I've been using Duolingo since 2012 and have recommended it to countless people. To see the app stoop to this level is disheartening to say the least. "Free" doesn't really mean free anymore if you're shoving annoying ads for bad quality content in our faces.

The last update ruined the whole experience. It has become really annoying because it seems to be more about watching ads than learning a language (in the free version). Can't earn hearts by exercises anymore! Instead one has to watch nonsense ads?! Seriously?! Wish I could uninstall the last update. Maybe iy's time to try another app?! And I don't care for the whole AI stuff.... it used to be a nice app, it isn't anymore.

I am loving learning French with Duolingo, and have been for the past year. The reason for only 3 stars is because of the ads. I accept the need for them for a free app, but it's the same advert repeatedly. This has the opposite effect - repetitive ads on TV make me determined not to buy the product! Please at least vary the ads! Edit. 6 months later, and still the same ad. A little variety would be nice.

Overall fine, but the app wouldn't even launch today, and upon redownloading it, I can't log back in. It says that my email address that they're sending emails to doesn't have an account, or it logs in but it isn't the right account. I have cancelled my subscription and will have to start again. Duolingo has a problem with contact and support. I emailed a year or two ago for account/subscription suspension when I got a concussion and was never responded to. Guess I'm going to have to start over.

Thanks for bringing back the watch ads to get hearts option. Best update ever. Please add more German lessons. I've reached the end and keep on redoing old lessons and the daily challenge, but need new lessons to learn new words, etc. Ideen mit Bea sometimes has the wrong sound effect at the end when she chooses to work or not to work with the guest's idea. Some podcast lessons have a weird American accent put on while speaking German. Really off putting and just weird. Please stop that.

Every update seems to remove more and more quality of life features in an attempt to push you towards taking the subscription. Overall, I recommend DuoLingo for up to Pre-Intermediate French and for mostly Basic Dutch. Later, I'll try other languages. Thanks for all your hard work.

English is American English, so have to use American English words which is very frustrating and sometimes confusing. Spanish isn't European Spanish and you can't choose which version you learn. Can get very repetitive. it doesn't take the time to go through basis on how verbs work, or run through the numbers. just a different approach.

won't stop saying "You are offline" when i'm very clearly connected. have tried multiple different networks and none worked, Including 4G. even when i did manage to do my lesson, It didn't register it as done and didn't continue my streak. super glitchy, Please let me know how to fix this. update: I tried uninstalling and reinstalling, Worked for one day, stopped working. in anyways this app is filled with mispronounciation when it comes to japanese. i have better apps, like for example, renshuu

Scoring doesn't work sometimes despite what points it tells you that you can get and has been like this for a good while. Last night, my first lesson for the week, I did 3 triple XP lessons which should have been around 300 points. I looked on the scoreboard at the end and I have 80 points. Very very frustrating. As a positive, the improvement to watch ads to earn hearts makes the free app usable again but I already got into using another app because the recent lack of ability to earn them

it used to be perfect before they added the ads. instead of practicing to refill hearts you have to eat h an ad now!? I got 3 ad's one after another even though I had a perfect lesson and got everything right. I swear it's gonna get to a point where you have to watch an ad before a lesson, I used to love this app now it's just becoming like all the other apps that spam ads. Hope it doesn't get worse from here

what was once a great learning tool, is now almost entirely unusable. at the end of every exercise (that takes a minute or two to complete) you have to sit through 2 adverts (one for an upgrade and one for some random product) all the best tools for revising are locked behind upgrades and you can't even 'master' a lesson without paying 100 gems per attempt. and I had super for a year and instead of getting ads for super, they started giving me ads for max. not worth the time anymore.

I was enjoying this app with a Super Duo subscription for last year. Then, I decided to subscribe to Max to have speaking practice. It cost much more expensive and I am totally disappointed by this version. Only one option added to call with Lily and it really one sentence with no feedback. I tried a few different apps that offer speaking with AI and it much-much better. In my opinion, the cost of Duo Max doesn't make any sense. I am going to unsubscribe the Max.

Used to be a good app but now there's 2 ads after every level, 1 real ad and another ad about "super duolingo" which is so overpriced, and they've also introduced a new subscription tier which is double the price and only gives you like 2 features, one of which is the video call feature which is incredibly glitchy and really bad. she takes overly long to reply and you only get 2 sentences before she hangs up, and sometimes she doesn't respond and just keeps nodding

The app is better than ever. I've been a user since 2013, and I am really happy with how it has evolved. BUT I can't stand the ads, having 2 advertisements after each lesson is just too much, and I don't find all the features of the super and ultimate plans that appealing. I'd love to have an offer for a "lite" plan with no ads and no promotions for the higher tier plans, and maybe faster heart recharges (no infinite so it's challenging) for maybe 12 euros per year.

Good app when it wants to be. Way too excessive with the ads. It turns into nearly every minute. My biggest dislike is the way you get questions wrong supposedly if there spelt wrong. As someone who's always struggled with grammar and spelling since childhood doing it in a different language is not as easy to remember. While at the same time I understand if a words completely off that's fair but one letter off is way too over the top. I'm not doing the Spelling Bee.

as someone with not a lot of time duolingo became unbearable to use due to the long ads about super EVERY lesson. i understand the developers need the funds for their livelihoods and to fund the app, but the subscription is too expensive compared to my country's currency so I cannot pay for it. I understand the ads but I think it's a bit too much.

I cannot in good conscience rate a learning app that prioritizes profit over accuracy. I'm using it to refresh my Japanese, and the amount of mistakes is disturbing. E.g., differentiating between lunch box and lunchbox to fit their format, or using ai-voices that don't use the correct pronunciation (which in Japanese can be the difference between 'oo' and 'tai'). If they would only read the reports and check with someone competent....

It's today my 365 day streak in Duolingo, and I'm very much disappointed that a lot of features that were always free, are now paywalled. You have to either pay for the subscription or pay a lot of crystals. I understand making new features like ai studying help or whatever accessible only with the Super subscription, but not the old features... It's even more dumb, considering there is no method to buy the subscription in my country

best language learning app I've come across, I'm so happy with it. It takes me step by step in the learning experience of new language, repeated tests in different ways to make sure you memorise everything, it's so amazing and I love it, however I am not so happy with the all-time adds popping every now and then , as I can't afford to buy the app now. but other than that it's the best app ever

TL;DR Was good; won't renew! No longer seems to be a way to turn off lessons such as Music or Math. Song progress is gone as is pretty much all previous music, even Hotcross Buns has a slower tempo along with new accompaniment. Wouldn't mind the new music if I could have kept the old. Math matching is broken: have to go super slowly to avoid false matches. Stories (German) keep being moved; can't tell which have been read. Finally, the constant pressure to buy the AI driven Max!

there is no offline version, cant tell what i was supposed to learn, too vague, the ads are very weird, disturbing and cause stress with flash or little characters dying, i cant handle depressing ads or flashing ads or utter rubbish straight after being in the learning zone. i really dont care about points, i want to do lessons continuously with no distractions, most lessons are so repetitive i learnt nothing after a 870 day streak, then gave up. Never skip to higher levels its very unorganised

The user experience used to be solid, but now it has gotten much worse. Especially with the desperate Duolingo ads after every lessons! I understand the third party ads but do you really need to advertise your own service so often? This makes me wonder what are the alternatives for Duolingo? Also, when listening to sentences, there should always be an option to slow it down as it's often almost impossible to understand what you are hearing.

Good to start but: 1) not enough explanation of the rules 2) They have introduced a higher tier for AI explanations - which I refuse to upgrade as I see it as moving the goal posts in a cheeky way 3) the time based rewards encourage people to not spend enough time learning properly but to rush through it to get points. i liked it initially but now I start to see its limitations when trying to seriously learn a language.

Everytime I open the app, it says "Duolingo wants to send you practice reminders". I have used the app every day for several years without ever using practice reminders, without using the widget, without allowing notifications. I have always had notification features off and yet this banner keeps showing up everytime I open the app. Please remove the banner. Not everybody needs constant marketing in order to learn a language. If this is a permanent feature then I'll find a new app.

it is good if you want to properly learn a language. But if you just want a casual experience, like learning essential phrases and words for traveling, then it is not great. I'm also not sure how it handles other languages, but for Korean, AI voices pronounced some sounds and words inconsistently.

Dont like the app comparing me with beyonce. Dont like leaderboards. Exercises repeat with too much frequency. Edit: units just teach like 1 or 2 things. I often can skip 80% of the unit because it's all repeat repeat repeat. It's like the app thinks you are dumb or something. Translation using the word bank doesn't teach you at all because you can guess the whole sentence. After a 600+ days streak I can tell you that you will learn much better Japanese with Renshuu.

The app lacks the option for Spanish to be taught in British English (I don't want to learn about my 'mom' who eats 'candy' whilst watching 'soccer'!!). Also, the Spanish taught is Latin American NOT Castilian as spoken in Spain. As a Brit, the latter has more relevance for me, so the option would have been good. The app is 'fun' but fails as a serious teaching aid as it doesn't explain enough and you're left repeating rather than understanding the sentence structure. I've switched to Babbel.

Two points: 1. No grammar explanation in some cases. In terms of functionality of the app it's nothing, you just need to add more explanations for every section. 2. Explain to me the point of 2 Match exercises. I understand why the app forces you to pass this exercise, you need more engagements, but why do you think that this exercise teaches anything? Absolutely useless exercise and I hate when the app forces you to pass it.

Used to be a 5* review. App has gotten worse with time. I don't mind ads that help pay for free lessons, but duolingo doesn't use ads, it uses unskippable animations to annoy its users into upgrading. There's many ways to incentivise a purchase, like adding extra features, instead you have to pay for the "privilege" of not being harassed. Digital equivalent of mafia protection money. Make users pay for the good things, not to avoid the bad things 🙄

GREAT EXPERIENCE! 4 months in and I already knew how to start conversations in my chosen language to study. HOWEVER, whenever I try to start a lesson, it would always hit me with a "No Internet Connection".
