Our network strength isn't that much of an issue because I can use apps that require more internet hassle-free. So whenever I try to take a lesson I would have to wait 5-10 minutes just to begin. It has already been like this for the past few weeks and it's beginning to get under my skin.

The time to earn stars is way too short especially when the voice detection doesn't work 100% of the time. Voice detection will sometimes refuse to recognize names. Other than that it would be a great and fun way for learning many languages and now even music and math fast.

The streak freeze function is atrocious aand can not be turned off. The streak freeze function ruined every genuine attempt I to made to achieve a streak by punishing me with days of waiting until the freezes run out and the streak finally resets itself. There is no way to reset a streak yourself. There is no response from support after many days and many attempts to contact them There seems to be no way available to contact a human who works for duolingo for help.

I think it's incredibly stupid that hearts take 5 hours to recover 1 and that it's stupid how it costs 100 gems to take legendary levels but it doesn't refund you if you cancel the lesson. double ads at the end of lessons. edit: exp potion bugs. when I complete two quests at the same time it only gives the first reward. it says quest completed but no double exp. what's worse is when the next day triple exp doesn't activate. please stop wasting my time Duolingo.

DO NOT START ANY FREE TRIALS Started a free trial whilst on holiday. Cancelled the free trial well in advance of the end date, but Duolingo have made it so that cancelling a free trial isn't the same as cancelling the upcoming subscription. Because they charge on an annual basis, they have used this misleading design to steal £60 from me. Special note to the Google Play team who were also useless on this matter - do not expect any help getting your money back from this company.

It's very very useful and funny app.I liked The characters' interaction when you answer right or wrong 🤣🤣. And I also liked the widget of your daily active,it makes me go to the app and take a lesson to not lose my stroke😂 Third thing is the multiple languages,there is a lot of languages that makes me training on more than one language. THANK YOU "DUOLINGO"

too much gamification and also a longstanding bug where the app prefills some answers for you. why pay for something that doesn't even do its job of teaching? also, now at night if I don't do a lesson on my phone, the app icon turns angry (even if I did lessons on another device!) Like, what's the goal here? constant use? cmon! bugs: incorrect sound effects in podcast lessons, plus "show" is always one of the words to guess in the podcasts. AI slop, anyone?

Duolingo needs better UI designers for accessibility. Their icon graphics, which are an attempt to be funny, are actually anxiety inducing for some. Real people have anxiety disorders and images which induce panic (referring to eyes bulging out, dead, dying) because it's later in the day is not a great image for those folks. Better images for app use reminders could be imagined.

It's good, amazing infact. But would make it perfect if they added the video call feature for non-pro users too! It would be a five star then,and also there's so many extra features for the pro version....But not the non-pro version. It would be great if they balanced both of them together.And would just make slight difference.

I play and there are scores for each game, but after playing, my total score does not add up correctly, there is always a huge reduction affecting my promotion in the league and invalidating my efforts. The developers need to look into this. It has been going on for a while now, about 2 months. imagine playing everyday and your scores are always reduced terribly, how happy would you be to continue playing?.

5 Refresher course is a terrible idea. and a 1 minute ad after every single lesson is such a disappointment. This app is not free, it consumes your time with lengthy ads and unnecessary refresher course, and encourages you to pay a subscription through super duolingo. Sure, you'll learn a few things about the language you want, but they make it too long to actually "learn" more because of ads and unnecessary refresher courses again and again and again. Mizu to Gohan Kudasai is insane.

I'm absolutely loving Duolingo. The app is super engaging, fun, and effective. The bite-sized lessons make learning a new language a breeze. I really love the French lessons and the music lessons as well. I highly recommend Duo to anyone who wants to learn another language or music.

I decided to learn a new language and this app is helping a lot. Is easy to use and the plus version allows you to study even offline. Perfect for me, since i work in a place with no internet connection. But it doesn't make any distinction from português and Brazilian, which are similar but different. Also some of the phrases that teaches you make no sense and are bit random. One thing I really don't like are the extremely passive aggressive tones of notifications to "motivate" you learning.

I love this app. keeps me engaged. Offline mode would be awesome, though. When you are learning a different language on a mobile app, the distractions are plenty, even more so when you're online. Also, for a guy like me who's from Africa, I don't always have access to reliable internet, and when I do, the distractions earlier mentioned flood my phone. Thus, my progress is deterred. But let me not give excuses for my lack of commitment. Great app!

Duolingo used to be an incredible app — fun, accessible, and genuinely motivating for language learners of all levels. I would’ve happily given it 5 stars not long ago. But unfortunately, everything that made it great is now locked behind an increasingly expensive paywall. The free version has been stripped down to the point where it feels more like a frustrating demo than a real learning tool.

I've been using Duolingo for a month now and I absolutely love it! It's such a fun and effective way to learn English. The lessons are short and easy to follow, and I really like how it feels like a game. It keeps me motivated every day with rewards and reminders. I’ve already learned so much vocabulary and grammar, and I can see my progress clearly. The app makes learning feel fun, not stressful. It’s the best language-learning app I’ve ever used—definitely deserves 5 stars!

very useful as duo keep reminding me with notification. it's not easy to learn a language that's why is important to practice everyday or at least 5 days a week. Duo lingo not only pops up in notification but it actually sends me email to remind me with cute emojis..I really appreciate it, looking forward to upgrade to Duolingo max when I get the chance.

I have been on this app several years with over a 1k day streak. I see some updates have happened as far as animation. Sadly, this came with a Hefty price increase in gems. No one asked for this! Completely unnecessary. This should be student (budget) friendly and it is NOT. Needless to say, the amount of work you need to earn gems now it's ludicrous. This is still an app for education and learning and Duo keeps killing the motivation . Way to go 👎🏻

Nice app! Would really like to have expanded feature of drawing letters/symbols like in japanese hiragana/katakana. S pen works really good but it would really shine if you could practice drawing more than once and repetitively as well as without the automated guidelines so you coul draw it more crudely to practice form. Dropped it to 2 stars because Duo is interrupting every lesson 2 times with annoying sound. Kanji drawing is still broken

I am writing this review while I am on a 1993 day streak. Clearly I see some value in the app to keep using it. My issue is after many days I ended up buying the premium version just so I can stop the endless bombardment of "Upgrade now","Upgrade please" pop ups. Knowing I will use the app every day it was a purchase well made. However now I am being bombarded with another upgrade plan called "Max". It is not justifiable to still bombard your subscribers with ads after they pay. Unbelievable.

I like learning with duolingo, I am almost in the third year of paying for super, but the latest updates have been a pretty bad experience. The layout was changed too often and problems like the dark mode not working anymore for months now or randomly loosing friend streaks without reason are not acceptable.

as much as I enjoyed doing Duolingo for 20 days now, I hate how intrusive the ads are. it makes me discouraged from using it and encourages me more to use other resources like YouTube etc. I don't need to be reminded about Super Duolingo every time I finish a lesson, just make it once a day and that's cool already, as if the ads aren't annoying enough lol. i am currently looking for an alternative Duolingo because of the ads now

The Super version helps with learning. I like the listening practice and the vocab practice. The free version is frustrating as you are allowed no more than 5 mistakes, then a long wait to reset, so not enough practice to learn a difficult language. It's a shame they got rid of the grammar tips they used to have. Now you really need a book as well for reference, or a person who can explain the rules a bit. Otherwise it's frustrating trying to guess why an answer is marked wrong.

It's a good application to start learning multiple languages with different exercises such as writing, speaking and listening. However, it's getting increasingly difficult to use it as a non-super user (free). A few weeks ago it was still possible to replenish multiple hearts by doing special exercises. Then it got limited to one heart and now you have to either pay, get duolingo super or watch ads. It's quite unfortunate what the need to earn more and more money does to good things.

I am ready to change the review but right now I am not happy with the app. Suddenly my spoken exercises cannot be done, app just makes a noise, says try again and there's not even a possibility to try. Nobody answers when I send a report about this. I have a payed family plan and nobody from Duolingo helps to solve the problem.

Overall the app is great. But of course with learning any new language, other resources are needed (podcasts/movies/books etc). There is a bug where it sometimes won't pick up what you're speaking. It's definitely a bug because it won't even pick up my native French wife's speaking. I would love to see more stats and be able to categorise the words you've learnt by verb, adjective, noun etc. I would also love to see more explanations/theory rather than just game-like exercises.

Subject: Issue with Listening Exercise in Unit 9 (Social Media) Dear Duolingo Support Team, I am experiencing an issue with the first listening exercise in Unit 9 (Social Media). The audio clips do not match the displayed words, making it impossible for me to complete the exercise and progress to the next stage. I have tried refreshing the page and restarting the app, but the problem persists. Could you please look into this issue and provide a solution? Thank you for your support.

The app has a lot of ads, which is very frustrating when trying to learn. However, if you think, "Okay, I'll spend some money for education," you quickly realize that it becomes outrageously expensive. Because even though you pay 15€ for Premium and no ads, you still can't access everything. For that, you need the affordable Duolingo Max for 30€. It leaves you speechless. However, the design and learning content are well done, and you can learn quickly if you want to.

It's simple to use. The way that the lessons are structured also amazing. Yet I'm a bit disappointed with one of the learning method in which we need to write down the exact translation. For example in Indonesia: "Saya ingin mencari petunjuk arahnya" apparently need to be translated to "I want to look the directions up" which doesn't make any sense. "I want to look for the direction" is just fine yet the system sent an error mark.

Agree with a lot of the other reviews. As of spring 2025, functionality with a free account has become very limited. Repeating already learned content has become quite inconvenient, making it harder to do two languages at once, but also more difficult for me to remember everything from only one language course. I loved the option to be able to earn hearts by reviewing older lessons, but that seems to be completely gone. I learn less, have less fun with the app, and spend less time on it.

Really liked the app, even decided to pay a subscription and used it happily for 4 months. Today, I found out that Duo skipped 8 (!!) units in my German course, and there is no way of redoing those normally, only reviewing. Now, all my progress is messed up, and I am left with a huge gap in my knowledge. As a result, I had to delete the course and start all over again because the course has also changed, and units I learned before are all different. This is very demotivating.

It is a very useful and fun way to learn a language for many reasons: for business, for travel and even for fun! However, without either a Duolingo plan (costs money) or some other form of spending, it is difficult to learn a lot of a language quickly if you are going to the another country in a short amount of time. I really recommend getting the app because personally, it has been helping with my Spanish fluency a lot for my upcoming visit to Barcelona.

It's fun to use for the first ten minutes. Then ads appear and they stick around. Could not get back to the app even after waiting ten minutes. I purchased "Hearts" from the app, but that didn't help the issue. The style of learning a language is not well organized. Verb conjugation is never explained. You are just told that you got it "wrong"...how can you learn from that?

I love the app in general, I think it's really good. However, the 1 ad takes longer to watch than completing 1 lesson, and it happens after every single lesson. It basically encourages you to pay for premium otherwise you just get demotivated by such long ads. Please do something about it, either reduce the amount of ads or reduce the time of these ads.

Overall Duolingo has been really helpful for me learning German, the little games are fun and it's really improved in terms of teaching method since I last used it. However, I am consistently having issues with the speech exercises... they are usually fine when in a general unit, but when you have to repeat the same sentence over and over, certain words will not be accepted. This is kind of weird because I have had sloppy pronunciation be acceptable and perfect pronunciation be unacceptable 🤔

It's a good app and quite helpful. If you already know the language or wish to perfect it, this is a great tool. It's a convenient tool to expand your vocabulary. I didn't give it 5 stars cause it seems to have a microphone issue lately, at least to me. It doesn't detect my microphone when I speak and immediately tells me I said things wrong. It's a shame cause practising orally is essential in learning a language.

With Duo you can learn a lot, but it can be slanted sometimes. I have learned a bit of the language before. I understand the way they speak in one country. The accent as well as vocabulary is quite noticeably another country. An example I was translating an exercise with a word not yet taught in Duo I used it from the country I know. Duo marked it as wrong. That can be extremely frustrating. I feel there are also still glitches in the app. Many times my "wrong" answer and the right are thesame

It's a good app for learning vocabulary, but I think it needs more practice opportunities. I’m currently in Section 1, Unit 5 of Chinese, and many vocabulary words/characters from earlier units no longer appear in exercises. Without consistent review, it’s hard to retain them long-term, especially as new units introduce more words. It would also be great to add mini-stories for listening practice.

A great app that I've been using for almost 9 years and am currently on a 375 day streak. However, they have introduced a bug that does not let the app to be used in dark mode. It used to be synced with the phone options, but suddenly stopped working. And the app settings have no option to change it. I will be using another app until they manage to fix the issue.

Lessons rely solely on context clues, many of which have multiple correct or plausible answers. Full of ads. If you want us to pay, just put a price tag on it. I also hate the streak system because it destroys your motivation to learn. I used to spend hours a few days a week learning lessons, but now I just do the one lesson a day to keep my streak. It just gets annoying, and I'm not motivated to take that initiative in my leisure anymore.

It was good for beginners, it helped me especially with japanese. The problem is, the voices are so incoherent, it's AI, that's why. Listening exercise became a distressing activity since it sound so incomprehensible. The lessons, words, topics and meanings are great, although needs to have some improvement since Japanese people doesn't necessarily use those words. And ads. Everytime I end a lesson ads popped up, no problem if every 2 lessons but no, it's every single time I ended a lesson.

Really great app... Except for the fact they recently lost their mission to make it free and accessible for everyone. After every single excercise (which lasts about 2 minutes) you get 2 ads, both lasting about 30 seconds each... great way to prioritize learning! Worst thing is the second is always the unskipabble add for super duolingo. I'm fine with a normal ad, but stop being greedy please and stop pestering people into paying 15 euros a month for the version without the super duolingo adds.

It is an amazing app. I have been learning Chinese for only three months but I know simple sentences now. I love this app! The only thing is that sometimes when you're doing a listening exercise, no sound comes out at all. Even when the volume is at its max. So, please fix this problem, Duolingo. I would really appreciate it. Edited: Yeah, someone really needs to do something about the problem of no sound coming out when I am learning! Like is it just me or do other people find that annoying.

There is an increasingly frustrating bug in the app that prevents choosing words from the word bank, with no way to progress beyond, resulting in a wrong answer each time, which then costs hearts. The bug persists now for months. As for the content of the app, it's very good for starting out, but once you get to late beginner or intermediate level on some languages, there is not enough explanation or demonstration of why certain grammar rules exist. That lessens the value of the app.

Great app for practicing languages, thank you!🧠 Would like to mention something that could be improved: In the music course when you need to tap the rhythm (especially double notes), it would be so much better if there were two buttons, because sometimes you can't catch the length of the note and rhythm at the same time using only one button

disappointing - at first this app is really quite good, particularly for introducing different verbs, tenses and vocabulary. Very quickly, however, the programme is repetitive to the point where you get something right because you had the same phrase or question only seconds ago. It becomes too boring to use. On the upside it's OK for the very basic foundations of a language and you can learn several languages at the same time. also watch out as payment is not monthly but one lump sum.

I resumed learning on Duolingo this year after a 2 years hiatus. I met quite a number of new features and I must say it's harder to miss a day's practice now. Kudos to the Duo team. However, the new app feels very buggy. Sometimes, the audio function doesn't work, so I can't listen to lessons and sometimes, I'm unable to start a new lessons because it keeps loading. I was expectantly waiting for a new update but none of the issues was fixed in the update.

It gets you learning. I wish I could turn off streaks though, it drives me nuts. I am more likely to do a long session every few days, rather than a little every day. But when you do that, the app bombards you with messages about losing your streak, which is very counter motivational. I know how Duo would respond, but I know quite a few people with a 200 plus day streak, because they do one minimum lesson a day. They can't functionally use the language they are studying though!

There's a technical problem with the App. (Spanish from German). I was a beginner when I started learning Spanish. First I was placed too high in the learning path abd had to learn grammar that belongs to a much higher level (B1-B2). I did levels 1-3 and suddenly was thrown back in a different level 3, which was more appropriate for beginners. I did this level too 2 months ago and I can't proceed to level 4. I wrote Duo 3 times, but no one cared to solve the issue.I am totally disappointed.

Too repative and easy. You can guess most of the answers by process of elimination and it reinforces bad habits. The radio sections are very boring and you are unable to skip the intros and outros. Not good if you are in a rush. mine seems to be stuck in a loop and not teaching me anything new and repeating the same stuff again and again. Im paying and still getting adds for Duo max. Very annoying! every other level is a duo max level. The video game sections could be more exciting.

The app is really good overall. It is interactive, fun, engaging and game-like, as the advertisement once stated. I recommend that the Korean course is reviewed, as it seems a bit less visual compared to the courses in other languages. Another suggestion I have is for the app to maybe include some more languages, like widely spoken West African languages. Aside from these, the app is one of the best when it comes to learning new languages.

Psychologically, duolingo has absolutely the best approach in learning foreign languages, but it has a huge flaw which are the ads. If you don't pay for the "premium" version of the app, you end up with insufferable ads after every single lesson. Not only do you have to watch random ads, but after the random ad, you have to watch duolingo's as well. I get that they have to promote themselves, but does it have to be that extensive? It just makes me want to delete the app and give up.

>900 day streak here: Duolingo gets worse with every update. It was never the best way to learn a language, but was a fun way to build a habit. However over the years they have restructured the learning paths many times, each time resetting my position in the tree and confusing what I have and haven't already done. The new addition of largely AI-generated activities has also led to a slew of low-effort, often incorrect roadblocks that pad your time on the app. Don't bother with Duolingo in 2025.

This app use to be useful. But suddenly it thinks it's my first time using it, lost all my progress for some reason. Then to top it off, it doesn't hear me verbalise the tasks it asks, I have a brand new phone that works perfectly for everything else, but anytime I try to repeat the sound for words/sentences it always cannot hear me. I'm constantly set back due to how the app works now. Before, you could choose skip verbal until you wanted to. But now it's mixed. So you must pay to avoid this !

Tasks where you need to construct a sentence out of words is bugged. Half of the times it refuses to insert any word (its font changes colour to red). The only fix is going to main screen and then back in the app. It makes time-restricted tasks nearly impossible to complete. Extremely annoying. Everything else is fine, but I'm a perfectionist. Inability to complete all tasks drives me crazy.

It's just not what it used to be. They're removing more and more free features to force you to pay for their premium subscription. Hearts take too long to recharge, there's no explanations of sentence structure or grammar, and some courses don't have much content (Spanish has a whopping 8 sections, while Finnish has only 2). The news about staff being let go to be replaced with AI is disappointing as well, and is not a good look for the company as a whole. I'll be looking for another app.

Absolutely zero customer service for problems, even if you're a long-term paying user. It's not good for trying to learn, ok for refreshing. They used to provide lessons, but you have to pay extra for that now on top of the pro membership. it's not worth it. I had an almost 3 year streak as well in the top league... it dropped off incorrectly, and I lost the whole streak. there was nobody I could talk to about it. that upset me, so now I'm cancelling my subscription and going elsewhere.

Duolingo is a fun and interactive language-learning app. With its gamified approach, learning feels more enjoyable. It offers a variety of languages and exercises, including reading, writing, listening, and speaking. However, grammar explanations are limited, and some features require an internet connection. It's great for beginners who want to learn in a casual way!

Love it. It helps me me keep motivated, especially with Duo as a widget on my home screen. Being the competitive person that I am the streak thing really keeps me going. The app moves at my pace and is repetitive. It was kinda annoying, but then I realised that if things weren't repeating so much, I would have forgotten!! soon, I can proudly address myself as bilingual!!

It's a good app to learn languages. But it does have bugs. The most irritating bug is when you loose gems on missing a streak. And it's not possible to contact support even with a paid subscription. Duolingo should provide some avenue to report issues, at least for subscriptions. After the launch of Duolingo Max, the explanations are also very limited, so the app is not as good as it used to do earlier.

The free version is basically useless. There's an ad break after every lesson (Lesson. Not chapter) and wait for it... it gets worse. After the ad, there's another ad begging you to get the premium version of the app. Basically, 1 lesson... 2 ads. Every. Damn. Time. The ads take longer than the lesson! I know ads are a way of monetization, but this is too much

There needs to be a warning in the app about jumping ahead in the course because if you do this, then you will lose access to the tutorial material from the earlier sections, you'll only be able to practice them, for which the content does not give you the assistance that the tutorial material does. Aside from this one thing, this is a great app. The way out is to delete the course, re-add it, and then skip forward to where you were, but accumulated XP for this language will be lost.

It's a great app overall, really fun. But, there's one thing really annoying. Two, actually. First of all, my animation settings are toggled on, and yet the motion is still stiff, no animations shown. I believe it's a bug. Secondly, the ads are SO annoying. It just keeps popping up almost every time after I finish a lesson. Please, Duo, I don't have the money to buy your trial yet, so stop giving me your ads. Still a great language learning app, though.

they're pushing ads out that you can't close. horrible UX. I have to close the app and reopen it to get out of the ad. I have more frustration with the UX than I I have joy of language learning. I'm considering other options, some premium and free with my Library (I suggest others do the same). it seems the focus has shifted completely to making more money for the app, at the expense of user experience.

It is so user friendly and it makes learning entertaining, with its bright colours and animations I think even kids couldn't stop paying attention! 💯. Edit: Lately it's been having the issue that it doesn't recognize when I finish a lesson and it sets me back to do the same thing several times, I would really appreciate if that was fixed...

I've been using this for some time and can get past a few annoying glitches from time to time, but this last update removed the option (at least on Android) to turn on dark mode. I checked each setting, rebooted the app and took to the web to no avail. Now the screen is so bright it's annoying and makes me not want to use it. Especially when I'm in a dim lit room and now my screen is illuminating everything. If I've missed something, please let me know where to find the toggle.

This is great! It really helped me with speaking another language, the reason I'm giving it a three though is because of the limited hearts. It doesn't let you practice for any anymore. I was one question away from finishing a unit and I had one heart left, I got it wrong on accident and lost all my progress, now I have to redo the whole unit. It's just frustrating when you work hard and then lose it because of one question.

I really enjoy the app, it has a really easy way to progressively learn new things. But it is sad to see the greedy way the company is taking... Constantly pushing the paid version down your throat, is super hard to replenish your hearts now so you can keep learning. It's a couple of small things but it really is starting to take away from the experience

We enjoy duolingo app, especially now that my son has started learning how to play music on the app. But the music has changed. My son enjoys the piano music and the synthetic keyboard updated version is very distracting and does not help the player to follow the tune. He struggles to focus on the notes and it is playing faster than what it was before. Please can a option be made where one can choose the plain keyboard accompaniment. Thanks you.

1. It would be helpful to have some actual grammar and pronounciation teaching instead of leaving us to figure them out by the vocabulary presented. 2. Tips are occasionally shown but are on the screen so briefly I usually miss them. 3. Otherwise, I am really enjoying learning a new language via Duolingo. The lessons are fun and mistakes are reviewed at the end of each lesson. 4. For the best experience I would advise upgrading to paid so you can review mistakes and vocabulary.

Recently the reliability of doublers has been really bad. When you make the effort to send one to a friend or do the tasks to turn one on, it's really demotivating when it breaks. XP will also just disappear or not get counted in the first place. It's especially bad when it happens on a Sunday and it gets you demoted. Would really like to see developers work on making this more reliable.

The overall app is good and its user friendly interface makes it engaging. But the major cons are :- 1. Lessons feel way too repitative which is unnecessary. It's been a long time since I see no progress in my learning due to this. This needs to be fixed anyhow. 2. Exact meaning of each and every word is not given I don't think I'm going to use this app anymore bcs I see no progress at all due to repitative lessons and it is boring.

it's a nice learning app! funny and diverse characters ask you the questions. but not full stars because in several languages the words you learn in the first levels are not useful for daily life, and if you don't have the paid version there is a lot of annoying advertisement that you have to watch. in my opinion the paid version isn't good enough for what you get, and there is no option to have a monthly subscription.

I think it is a great way to learn a language. my child who is 8 is even learning through it. however, there are things which are not appropriate in our culture. I subscribed in Duolingo max, but I think I will cancel it. explain my mistake feature is good, but the AI is not good at all. conversations are too short and are irrelevant to the topic of the unit.

Amazing app! Really makes learning enjoyable. The paid version looks to have some really awesome benefits. If you're someone who is interested in languages or intends to travel, it would potentially be worth upgrading! But the free version is good too. It just limits your mistakes, you then have to wait to retry the quizes. The paid version gives you unlimited mistakes. Either way, super cool app!

It's a very accessible, well put together app. Two main recommendations: 1. Translating sentences into your own language is somewhat useful. However, would it be perhaps more prudent to get the learner thinking in the foreign language more often? This isn't as easy, but it provides a learning curve which may be more beneficial in the long-term? I may be wrong on this one. It will be interesting to see what research says on the matter. 2. There's no explanation of the grammar. Word limit :(....

Duolingo has been my go-to learning for more than six years now and I have often been in the top 2-3% of learners at the end of each year. I didn't mind watching ads when necessary and I appreciated that ad revenue was what supported the app, but in light of the recent changes (no longer being able to practice for hearts and onger ads) I find myself more frustrated with it than anything. Sorry Duo, my streak ends here :-(

I downloaded this app and took the free trial for a month and paid for the yearly subscription, When it was the end of the trial month i had paid for it with no warning email sent to me, this was upsetting as i was planning on using the money for my weeks groceries. I emailed them with everyone telling me it was a waste of time, but still did and was quickly refunded and had my subscription cancelled. Great customer support.

I've began using Duolingo since the last year to learn German and it's really effective and improving my learning. The daily tasks help to keep me determined. But, I've come across an error recently; there is another type of translation exercise and of course there are words to use. Although, when I try to do it, it doesn't work and I get stuck on that particular excercise. It frustrates me as I have to exit, and I lose my short progress. Please look into it. Overall, a fun learning app! :)

I really like the app and use it daily - although progression can feel slow, I personally like the repetition for the most part. Unfortunately the ads recently have been getting more egregious, and I understand that's the cost of a free version, but when Duolingo's own ad for it's premium version openly mocks the quality of the other ads the app shows, that leave a bit of a bad taste

This is the best language learning app ever. They simplify the class in a way that even a language novice must understand it. I never had a background in Spanish, but now I see my self speaking some of the basic words. If you are seeking an app to help with ur language learning, I recommend Duolingo, it has been tested and trusted. The only problem with it is that very early in the morning it's like the system crashed, but after some hrs like around 10/11 am (WAT) everything is back to normal.

Update: There is now a dedicated section to practice learned words with the frequency and success rate accounted for. Nice one Duolingo! My main gripe now is ads for 'MAX' despite paying for 'Super' already. 2019: Not without its issues but super fun and addictive. I wish there was a list of words learned available in each section. sometimes the random generator will end up giving you the same phrase 5 times in a row and that tricky one you want to learn you never see again.

I genuinely don't understand how this game is supposed to help you learn a language. I've been taking many languages under my wing during my almost two years of 'learning' in total. here's my take on things. 1. Quite annoying. lessons are boring, and don't teach you a lot the communication in language itself. LARGELY missing the point 2. Skips many steps. while I was learning korean, I was having a hard time because they kept going over easy concepts intensively and skipping the harder ones.

Duolingo has helped me learn French very well. It makes me excited to learn more. I would give it five stars, but there are some downfalls. Firstly, the ads. Its not that big of a deal, but they are annoying. Secondly, the whole hearts thing makes you feel pressured and when you lose them all, its really discouraging. Otherwise, I do recommend using duolingo.

The app is serviceable but extremely buggy, both in terms of learning (pronunciations are accepted as long as you make similar sounds without saying a word and any stroke will be corrected regardless of whether you learned the correct character as long as it's in the right order so you really don't learn properly from it) and their reward system (which fails to retain data when you refresh the app). As best as could be expected from AI learning, good for practice but don't pay for it.

Uninstalled it, now that it's no longer dark theme. Loved the idea of learning how to read musical notes but the amount of notes and speed of playing increases way too quickly. It's just frustrating. The threats imposed by the owl are disturbing. I thought this app was supposed to be fun? What even are the pictures at the end of a lesson? They are nothing short of creepy. Guess that fits their strange image. There are way better learning apps out there.

Humbly I must say that it's not the beat choice for learning a language. Old text book style is even better. However it is BRILLIANT to expose people to something. Opening a book can be overwhelming, duo gamifies learning which is always great. It also help you understand the basics of how hard a language is / how to speak or write it so that you can decide whether or not it's for you. Personally don't think you can perfect a language from it as someone who's living abroad and learning with duo

This app is becoming more about profits and less about actual learning. They keep removing the option to practice - a huge component of strengthening launguage learning progress - for "hearts," effectively stopping free users in their tracks. What once was a tolerable amount of advertising is becoming overwhelmingly unpleasant. I was in the top 1% last year and was recommending it to my friends but I can't recommend it anymore. I'm now considering other resources instead. Sad to see it, duo.

One can always complain, but this app is golden. I have learned the basics for communication in other languages with it, and although it can always be better, it is understandable how good it is for something we don't have to pay for. I have two requests though: 1. Please eliminate the "no errors challenges", they are very frustrating and do not encourage participation, on the contrary, it makes people abandon the friend challenges. 2. Please bring back the "practice to earn lives"🙏🏻

I've been using this app to learn Hindi for a week, even without the Super Duolingo mode, and I absolutely love it! I highly recommend it to all beginners—the learning method is simple and effective, the graphics are engaging, and the reminders are helpful without being annoying. The overall experience makes language learning enjoyable. Looking forward to completing a full course!

It's good tool to learn languages. It can be fun but its shotcomings are sometimes very frustrating. Voice recognition is still weak. Also it teaches some useless stuff and it's missing proper structure. But I guess with leagues and achievements, they try to make it more a game than serious learning tool. It also cheats you out of XP multipliers if you seem too good or gaining too much. Multipliers time out quicker than advertised or they are never applied at all.

For some reason I keep coming back to this app and this time I love it more than ever. I really like the silly little skits and characters, I might cringe once in a while but it makes learning fun and light-hearted, which is weirdly soothing in a way? I don't know how others feel but the French course has been fantastic so far. I'm saving some money to get Super now since I enjoyed the free trial. Only complaint: maybe calm down with the ads a little bit. Keep up the good work!

Pretty good language learning app. Helped me start with really easy exercises, which made it want me to go back to it. Does have a few downsides, though. Their help and service email doesn't reply back to you, as I've been waiting . Their system for logging in acts up, telling me my account doesn't exist when I try and log in on separate devices. I've lost over 300 days worth of streaks because of it whenever I break my phone. HOPING this review sparks Duo to look into it.

Loved this app when I first started using it, but, changes have significantly reduced my enjoyment. I would still prefer not to be in leagues. Not having the option to practice for hearts anymore is very 'money grabby' in my opinion. Moving features that were part of the free element away because they have added another level of subscription. Often not getting hearts back within the prescribed time. Rewards not being applied as expected. Don't think I will using it much longer.

A fantastic app, an easy way to learn a language. I love all the different characters, they are very funny. You can practise the words or phrases you struggle with, there is no limit on the number of times you need to hear something repeated, plus it has a slow down button which really helps when the phrases are longer or a bit tricky. If you want to learn a language stress free then this is the app for you, I absolutely love it .

Duolingo is engaging and fun app, but some changes are frustrating. They removed the ability to earn back all hearts through practice—now it's just one, and the wait time to get it back is longer, pushing users toward an overpriced membership. There's also no real grammar learning, which feels like a missed opportunity. Plus, the notifications are borderline gaslighting, making you feel guilty for not playing. While it's fun for vocabulary, these issues make it less enjoyable.

when you click the words in the example, they don't consistently show you the translation in every exercise. Also when you successfully complete a translation, it sometimes just says congratulations, it doesn't confirm what the translation actually was. Plus if I pay an annual subscription, 'Explain my mistake' button should be included. Asking for MORE MONEY AGAIN for core learning functionality is not right. that's the whole purpose of the app!!

I really enjoy learning on Duolingo, but ever since signing up for the Super Duolingo version of the app, I'm not getting the XP boosts like before. Even though I'm completing the missions and it says I have an XP boost for so many minutes, it just doesn't happen. It is incredibly frustrating every time I have a session at the moment, which is why I am only giving 2 stars. Very disappointed!!

This app is amazing! It’s so interactive and engaging that learning a new language feels exciting and rewarding. The challenges keep me motivated, and the achievements make progress even more satisfying. Learning in person can be intimidating, but this app makes it fun, stress-free, and effective. I’m so glad it exists—it has truly helped me improve!

I had this app back in 2019, when it was actually helpful for learning a language. I rejoined in 2023, and since then it's been getting steadily worse and is now unusable. They keep trying to force you to buy Super Duolingo by making the free version increasingly rubbish. It's filled with loud, annoying ads, it offers no explanations for errors unless you upgrade (therefore not allowing you to learn), and no longer lets you practice to earn hearts. I'm out.

Once upon a time I rated this four stars. The teaching is still passable, but all elements that used to teach theory (the community forums) were removed a year or two ago. Most frustrating, though, is Duolingo's approach to communications and notifications. At least the obnoxious characters can be switched off, but the notifications are still annoying and passive-aggressive. "You're scaring me, don't skip a day!" is tremendously snotty... particularly at 0620 in the morning.

App has continuously gotten worse over time by making free features paid, adding AI where it is unnecessary (such as to explaining the meaning of a sentence, which should be a basic feature and not AI) and having a very limited free experience. They recently changed it so that you can not practice to earn hearts, but instead you have to watch an ad. Importantly, even when Duolingo was much better, there are far better ways to learn languages. Only use Duolingo if you find it fun.

Literally my only gripe is while learning (Japanese) it asks "what do you hear?" And I click, think to myself that's what I hear but get it wrong. What really needs to be asked is "what is being said?" It's a tricky language but I've almost made a 100 day streak. I'm enjoying it a lot, some words are a little off sometimes but thankfully it's usually correct when there is a slow playback option. Overall for a free app it's close to perfect. Might look into premium when I'm able to afford it

Great quality app and animations. The bad: the amount of repetition is mind-numbing and kills my spirit. I learned the Japanese alphabet from another app and it took me a month, and I enjoyed it... I'm in my fourth month now in Duolingo and I'm about midway with the alphabet. And I hate it. I do one lesson a day just to keep my steak. The app asks me to answer the same questions way too many times. If there was a setting to reduce the amount of repetition, I'd do it by 50%.

Welsh course seemed great at first but don't don't waste your time. After spending over 18 months with this it decided to switch to a "daily refresh" which just repeats the same 20 words or so for ever. Seems like there's nothing left in the course, but there's no indication that the course is over. It has just "broken" but keeps prompting you to come back anyway. After talking to first language speakers I have realised that it inappropriately mixes dialects without any explanation.

Bought the paid version, it's ok. Some serious inaccuracies and inconsistencies with the material. It has encouraged my otherwise very reluctant offspring to take a consistent interest in languages. The "words" section has been stuck on a very small selection of words. In Spanish I find the stories somewhat infuriating, it relies on reading between the lines rather than actual language skills, not good for autistic learners. The pointless new animations are annoying and distracting

Review is for the Irish language.. the audio is often clipped, meaning the start or end of a word is inaudible. At times the pronunciation (or recording) is very poor. I'm using this as a supplement to my live Irish classes with native speakers, so I do know what the words should sound like. This could be a lot better and if it was I would be willing to pay for it. However, the subscription model - pay for a year up front - is too expensive. I'd prefer to pay on a monthly basis

I would give a higher review, but the most recent update is destroying my joy for this app. Ive been using Duolingo consistently for almost a full year, but recently I felt a big change. For one, dark mode just doesn't work anymore (probably something that they will patch), but the biggest thing is the ads. You would usually get one ad for the premium version of Duolingo a day (after the first lesson you do). But the new update shows an ad for Every. Single. Lesson. (So an ad every 2 minutes)

Not much has changed in the past two years. Lessons in Asian languages still a total disaster (sentences like "the wand chooses the wizard" instead of something useful). Ancient and ineffective learning methods - associative learning is only for beginner parts, later, you will waste your time endlessly translating absurd sentences, like above. Super is a waste of money. You are better off spending it on actual IRL lectures.

Love this app, but I find one of the recent changes irritating. The "5 in a row" or "10 in a row" pop-up in the middle of my lessons is super distracting. Please remove it!!! Other than that, I'm loving the app. It's absolutely usable even in the free version. Yes, there are ads and a heart limit, but honestly 5 hearts is all you need. I love the new lessons where it's a listening activity with a 'guest speaker' discussing their day. I do wish the friends quests were easier to complete though!

I personally benefited a lot from Duolingo for German, but many people find it repetitive and not functional, I think one should be attentive and careful with the tasks, so that you don't just do "correct" and "proceed" , rather you pay real attention to every word, how it is written etc and learn actively from it. then you can benefit good from Duolingo

This program is incredibly engaging and makes learning really enjoyable . The way it teaches is fun and innovative, which keeps you motivated to learn more . There's just one minor thing, the ads in the program are a bit frequent, which can be a little distracting . But that won't stop us ! The solution is simple: Subscribing to Super Duolingo removes all the ads, and it makes the experience better. 😊😊

The App has been crashing a lot recently eg I complete a lesson and it won't record it which is incredibly annoying for a paid app. The App is basically a glorified phrase book. It doesn't give you any information about grammar so you do need to use alternative sources to help with grammar. The voice recognition part seems quite good without too many glitches as opposed to some Language Apps.

After using it for more than several years with 589-day streak, I want to say that this app is useless. It does not teach you a language - its gamified model tries to keep you involved and answer as fast as you can. While running in pursuit of these achievements, I forgot to learn the language. Finally, I decided to completely uninstall it, remove my account, and get back to the classical, time-proven method, which gives better results. Using it with traditional learning did not work either.

It's amazing! I am learning Korean and German right now. it is so simple and easy to use. plans are offered but not needed to learn, and there are little ads. There are also streaks and goals that motivate you to learn at least once a day, and my progress is amazing. You can also skip too different categories if you are visiting a country and need basics. 5 Star app, great experiences, and never-ending opportunities. 10/10 would 100% recommend for anyone wanting to try to learn a new language.♡

There's been a change to the free to use settings, where it's impossible to keep your streak if you fail- unless you want as many adverts as it takes for you to complete your session without mistakes or you pay for the unlimited upgrade. It no longer feels like you're learning, you're just punished for not remembering the correct sequence to their answers

I think Duolingo is a great app for learning the basics, but it could really improve by adding more real-life English phrases. Many of the sentences feel unnatural or too formal, which isn’t how native speakers talk. It would be awesome if they added common phrases, slang, and idioms to help learners sound more natural. Another feature I’d love to see is an online chatting option, where users can practice with real people. It would make the learning experience more interactive and practical.

Now worse than ever before. They have taken away the option to practise and changed the way that the leagues work ( if they are real). I'm not interested in competition, I just want learn at my own pace. Guess I'm heading for the bottom league. Totally de motivated by it now. Impossible to make progress with free version now that you can't gain hearts by practising. Don't appear to get 5 hearts top up either. Making more progress now using Busuu.

I love Duolingo, except for one thing. I find it extremely discouraging that, if you are having a bad day and use all of your lives before passing a lesson, it doesn't count towards your streak. Yes, I know you can practice to earn 1 heart back (and if you don't pay it takes forever for tour lives to refill), and in that practice, you can make many mistakes until you finish, but by then, you're so frustrated you only finish that one lesson for the day. Failed practice should still count!!

The app itself is great, but the ads are a big No-No for me, (respectively) , hence the 4 starts. There's been some flaws to the app popping up, in one of the practice modes, whenever I'm learning Italian it gets stuck on Finnish, and when I'm learning Finnish, it gets stuck on Italian so it's hard to get in alot of each practice modes...

After abandoning this app for a few years and returning to it a few weeks ago, I am finding more and more ads after each lesson, including an occasional collection of Google pop up ads that make me feel like I have been transported back in time to 2005. I haven't yet found a way to get out of the pop ups; all other ads, you can close or skip past after about 30 seconds but these pop ups just kind of trap me in an overlapping layer of links and I end up having to close the app. Hate that.

I am in 8th std and I opted for French. Many of my friends parents had told me to go for a crash course, but one of my friends recommended me this app. And trust me, I have learned to introduce myself in French in just a week( in tuition, I would have taken two weeks). This is a great app for learning languages. A huge thanks to the creators. But, there is one problem... After completing an exercise, the app hangs and I have to reopen the app. Please solve this issue.

For some reason I haven't been been able to do the speaking exercises for a few months now. The app doesn't register when I'm speaking and the recording just shuts off a few seconds in. I've tried uninstalling and reinstalling the app but that didn't help. Other than skipping speaking exercises, not sure what to do. (I have a Samsung phone).

They implement a "pay-to-win" strategy on their minigames which I'm totally against, it's just a ploy to get you to buy more in-game currency. There is not enough variation in the lessons, I've been on section 2 of Japanese for ages because I'm so bored of it. There's almost 40 sections! It's as if it tries to keep you there for as long as possible so they can can get another year's subscription out of you. I'm only learning new words, hardly ever learning new grammar.

I'm currently learning Chinese, and it's going well. You can do a lesson a day, or spend more time if you can manage. The only complain I have, is that after you get an ad, you get another Duolingo Super ad right away. I understand that the service is free, but I don't need to be reminded of Super after every ad. I'm more than happy to sit through the ads that help support the service, but it's a bit much after a while.

Been using this app daily (paid subscription) learning French for 3 years. Last week the app lost my position in the course, and moved me to the very last lesson making it impossible to continue learning. Their support people are completely unresponsive - you get an automated brush-off email, but no assistance whatsoever. They are clearly not interested in helping their users. Summary: a good app, until it goes wrong, at which point you're on your own 🙁

I really like this app as a whole, and I was going to leave 5 stars, but the speaking lessons are why im giving 4 stars. It doesn't give you a correct answer if even one word isn't recorded correctly by the microphone. Another reason is when I deleted the app, all my progress on my maths course got removed, and my french and music courses are fine.

the app keeps getting worse and worse over time. it looks to become only about earning the money. Even though the app can be great,the heart system is not fun to continue the path of learning.. It pushes you down to do low level learning in order to try again.. Reported it, and many other things, and it hasn't been picked up. The basic structure need to be improved, especially the Spanish is very full of basic mistakes, and my family has even a different version while both are up to date!

I love this app. Unfortunately, it has not been working for me as of yesterday. I started to notice that the app will say you have double or triple xp for 10 or wtv min but then when I do the lessons it did not work. I also have a 463 day streak and I can't get access to the streak society app icon. I tried updating the app it did not work I installed and uninstalled it and now it won't even let me log back in. It's saying error please try again later. I'll be so upset if I lose my streak HELP!

I've been using this app for nearly 10 yrs, but it is time to give it up. It is clear Duolingo is spending more money on marketing, than on developing its language courses. And no, using AI does not count. It has been dumbed down a lot in the past years, and focuses on the competitive factor rather than on teaching you anything substantial. There are no grammar or sentence structure explanations, so you kinda just have to guess what is right

Got app 2 wks ago; after trying Super version for a week, the section where I could cancel it became "unavailable" until after they charged me £60. The app will also tell me "that doesn't sound right" before I've spoken when doing speech challenges; then I fail when pronouncing them correctly (screen recorded them). Streak freeze function doesn't work, have 2 equipped, but unable to use. £60 for this privilege.🙄 Words geared to USA only, so confusing to English speakers in other 95% of world.

Almost useless. It doesn't actually teach you how, as there are no actual lessons. Also, there is no button to turn off American words. Wastes so much time learning the wrong words, or making two translations per word in your head. Surely simple issues to address, ridiculously. The exercises are decent to keep things ticking over if you are already learning it properly but don't have time to study properly.

Duolingo is a great app. Very useful and efficient. However, there are some bugs. Pls check Mathematics Section 2 Unit 9 Match Madness. Eg: Say 2 is the correct answer; there are multiple options stating 2; now it keeps giving me incorrect until I reach the option (answer 2) that is paired up with the question of interest. Pls look into this. Thank you.

This review is for the Danish language. The Danish courses could really learn from the German courses. German uses animations that make it more engaging, the interface feels more polished, there are stories and hearing comprehension lessons, and they use real voices instead of Google translate. Danish sounds just like Google translate, and the words are often cut off. It talks way too quickly too, so you can't really hear the pronunciation well.

I gave in and bought 'Super' and actually I get good value from it. Not limited by hearts or ads I get hours of sessions. I would say, having started Italian from scratch and re-acquainting myself with French (which I previously studied for over a decade); it is not a great way to learn from scratch, there is not enough explanation of grammar and vocabulary. As an additional resource there is none better. The gamifying and competitive elements really encourage repeat interaction.

There's a lot I like about Duolingo and also a lot I don't. It's a great simple tool to help learning languages, but at times it's too simple - it doesn't explain the 'why'. I get that they need ads on the free version, but after every single lesson? It's infuriating. I don't like that you can't disable the streak feature - it actually makes me avoid the app so it doesn't make me feel bad for losing a streak. Nor do I want people congratulating me on 'coming back' every time I just open the app!

Super fun way to learn a new language but the amount of adds is kind of annoying especially for people with time limits on their devices. It also gets frustrating when you lose all your hearts and aren't able to continue on. I would definitely recommend this as a tool for learning because it helps you enjoy education without simple and pointless lessons! Unlike many games, I have found that doulingo is almost exactly as engaging as many adds and people say.

I like working with duolingo..it keeps you moving...but it makes it too competitive. I always feel rushed...some of us aren't so quick and just want to enjoy the learning experience. Let the competing be a choice. I personally am not bothered about coming first..I just want to learn. The good thing is by joining a subscription I can get plenty of practise....

This language learning app is the greatest I have ever seen. One major problem is that although it will show you what the price for super is per month but only paying for a year is available. This could prevent many people from purchasing, including myself. Please add a monthly subscription option for family plans etc. and I will jump on that immediately. Thank you.

Great app for learning overall. I love the games and radio lessons. More of these please!! However, disappointed that only some languages seem to offer these (hoping that changes). I could also do without so many notifications. I could turn them off but I don't want NO notifications- just one or two a day would be enough of a reminder. I also have the widget so maybe take that into account. In my notification history I have 8 from duolingo in the past 24 hours reminding me to learn.

It is great as a basic introduction to a language, but quickly does everything in its power to get you to go premium. If you get stuck on a particular phrase or grammar, you may use all your hearts within the same lesson, and be forced to use the freemium currency just to finish one lesson you struggled with. The app also does a horrible job of introducing grammar and throws you into challenges that you've never done before so you'll fail, just to pressure you into the premium model.

Unfortunately, I had to change my 5 stars rating from 2023, to a 3 stars rating for 2024-2025. There were some major changes to the app, that almost make me want to quit the app, altogether. I love learning languages through the app but all the changes make it really hard. There were used to have 15mn booster at the end of each chapter. Now, if we lose our 5 hearts, we can only get one back, instead of 5. RIDICULOUS!!! Please correct this & go back to the previous version.

Overall it's good but the way it teaches written language is frustrating and possibly flawed, it moves too fast. you'll get a guide for how to write a character once or twice and then it will give weak directional queues without any reference to the letter on the screen do you're forced to strain yourself trying to remember something you saw for. 3 seconds, two weeks ago. They also take way too long to integrate object associations so you can translate in your head faster

The lessons are useful, which is why I have purchased the app. The constant ads for family plan are distressing as I have no family. The constant insistence I commit to a learning streak is infuriating and demotivating. It is not healthy, ime, to do anything 7 days a week, without respite. I am learning through choice, no-one has forced me to do this. Nagging is demoralising for me, NOT encouraging or supportive. At least provide an option to turn this off!

I have used it for 3.5 months almost everyday. There is no grammar explanation even on a paid version. You pay for the "super" and they ask you to pay more to get explanation on your mistake. A very passive style of learning that does not help with speaking or understanding grammar but just repeating a lot of simple conversations. It's a great gaming style of getting acquainted to a new language but the actual learning is minimal. Switching to Languatalk.

My streak on it is 1750 days, because it used to be a great platform! idk if they have new management or what, but the user experience has become absolutely horrible. it's so clear they're intentionally making the free experience more gruesome, so as to bug people into buying a membership. instead, they're likely going to lose users all-around. It used to be clear that the main objective was language learning, and that showed up in everything, but now it's clear it's just about making money. 🤮

2022: 5* App. Lessons clear, fun & effective. Been using it for years now and it's improved on earlier versions since using in 2015. 2025: 3* Sandards have dropped dramatically. Ads really aggressive, too often & too long. No 'quick lesson' anymore, as you spend longer waiting for ads than you do learning. Only one error and you're 'out of hearts' then have to wait hours or watch another ad to continue. Can't even upgrade as app won't connect to play store. Not what it used to be.

I ABSOLUTELY LOVE THE APP!:D I love Duolingo because it helps me learn and talk with my Japanese friend! It's really fun and engaging. But there's an issue… For the third time now, my streak froze even though I completed my lesson on time. I did my lesson at 9 PM, but when I checked my widget at midnight, it showed my streak as frozen, like I hadn’t done it. This is really frustrating because I’ve been consistent, yet the app doesn’t register my progress correctly. Please fix this bug!☹️

The success criteria to meet daily chance is to do the ramp up challenge. I never do these as with my slow reading speed (dyslexia) I find it too hard to scan words to match. So I have to buy the very expensive "row blaster" to make it easier, but it still is too hard for me. This means I can't complete the daily quest, can't get the bonus multiplier for the next day, and so staying in my league harder. I am a max purchaser, the ramp is a greedy money grab taking advantage of my disability.

Predatory, uses really bad methodology to teach you when you're not a premium user. You can easily get stuck on a chapter with no easy way to learn from your mistake because, again, every basic feature is stuck behind a paywall. Once you've learned enough to get started the app is a set back on many aspects killing the fun of learning a new language. First few weeks/months don't suffer much from these issues as the content is generally easier, enjoy it while it lasts

I'm about to complete a year using the app everyday and meanwhile I cannot deny that it has helped me, it has a lot of problems and room to improvement. 1. If you don't pay you're gonna last forever to complete one single course. 2. Its learning process is slow and repetitive because it wants you to keep using the app forever. If you learn quickly you'll let the app sooner. 3. It has a lack of grammar lessons. The app is over-focused on vocabulary and you learn almost nothing of grammar.

It's great fun and you can chose any language. They rarely put ads in and everything is so easy to find. The issue with this is when it say 'Free trial for super duolingo' you have to put your details in but it's free? Why do we need to put that in? What if I forgot my password or something like that? Plus it says free ot doesn't charge anything so why do I have to put my details in? All in All. Great game.

Once upon a time Duolingo was a 5-star app. I paid for it for years and it was a great way to keep engaging with the language. Unfortunately over that time, despite a few interesting features that were added, so much of the best stuff has been taken away. Most egregious is the rampant push of "AI"-powered content, which is thoroughly unreliable and - at worst - they make you pay even more for. I miss what we used to have, Duo. You're techno-capitalist garbage now. RIP.

Helps out with practicing and not forgetting the language, but I wouldn't rely solely on it. It needs to improve the quality for Japanese language too. The Japanese lessons seem to be behind all other languages. Despite having many lessons, most only cover N5, which is the bare basics. Also, but very importantly, customer support is terrible! There's no email to directly contact them despite being a paid customer!

whatever people say, it's still a perfect tool for long-term learning, when you better take it slow and easy to get used to a new language. I use it for learning Arabic and it's one of my main tools for the language right now. after all, when it comes to languages, you can't use only one tool and expect any kind of unbelievable results. duolingo works perfectly in the purposes it's made for: steady and easy learning of basic structures and words from zero, with listening and speaking exercises

The start of my duolingo journey was fine. It descended once the amount of ad walls for each thing got added on or changed. They used to have "Practice to refill hearts". Now it's watch 30 seconds to get 1 single lousy heart. You fail the learning portion and forced to watch ads to refill for another attempt, from the beginning. It does not even account for the fact that you'e done attempts, just another money-focused function of the app. I recommend you uninstall the app.

I've been noticing more issues lately caused by simple errors. One example would be that the app sometimes prevents the full answer from being entered, likely due to word count limitations. Strangely, this issue never appears during the "fix error" stage—only when initially answering the question. This inconsistency makes the experience frustrating and disrupts the flow of problem-solving. I hope this gets addressed soon.

Duolingo is a great app for learning new languages in a fun and interactive way! The bite-sized lessons make it easy to stay consistent, and the gamified approach keeps learning engaging. I love the streak system and challenges, which motivate me to keep going. However, some advanced grammar explanations could be clearer, and the ads can be a bit much without premium. Overall, it's a fantastic tool for language learners!

This is a great app for learning, but my main problem with this.. Is the VOICE parts of language lessons, because it doesn't pick up any of my voice AT ALL, no matter how loud or close I am, it's always gonna take a dozen tries before it works. I just wonder if you could replace it with something more capable of functioning properly its role as to PICK UP YOUR VOICE.

The app itself is great, I love using it and learning French is made massively easier. Having just moved from an iPhone, the quality level between the Android and iOS App versions microphone understanding is huge though, my S25 Ultra struggles to understand my speaking when I'm getting the simplest expression exact. Very frustrating not being able to progress because the phone thinks I'm getting it wrong. I'm blaming the Android software and not the phone though, maybe I'm wrong?

Great app for learning 👌 I've been learning Russian for months to communicate with most of my family and understand them. Sometimes, they teach me some words, but when they leave, I always use this app. The reason I did a 4-star review is that I didn't really like the new update. I loved the old duolingo with stories and some characters moved. But now nothing moves. I was hoping to find the stories somewhere but it was gone. Please bring it back

At the end of some lessons, when youve got everything right, it challenges you with harder questions, usually three questions which can either be typed or spoken. I find these ones frustrating as they are usually the same question just worded differently and are hard to get right which then messes up your score. Why not just give one question rather than three that are similar that make you feel punished for doing well.

The app is great while you are using the free trial or if you can afford to pay for super or max. If you can't afford it, it's very discouraging to use and extremely frustrating. Almost impossible to keep your streak alive without max and the option to practice to earn hearts has also disappeared. The challenges are not fair between free and paid users they should be seperated as the paid users get a TON of major advantages allowing them to pummel the ones who can't afford it into the dirt.

In regards to the radio/podcast listening exercises, please add a skip feature for the pre- and post-ramble. It gets very grating being forced to listen to the same jokes over and over again. For example, with "Late Nights with Lin" I get so sick of hearing Lin talking about how much she loves naps. At least give an option to have these pointless rambles be in the course language. For example, I'm learning Japanese. So have the hosts speak in Japanese, not English, so at least its more practice.

Great app, doesn't just only help learn languages easily, but helps my attention with everything. It seems to make it easier to learn multiple languages, probably because of the cognitive stuff. Only downside is the amount of ads. I don't pay for premium and after pretty much every lesson it gives me an ad, usually temp and then a duolingo premium ad

Good - but stories end! Good language learning app but the developers have been lax in that they've started up stories--which are a great way to pick up new vocab and grammar but I got to the end of them relatively quickly and no more are available, which I think is pretty lame. Also, there's only so much annoying cutesy language, ridiculous intonation and talk of kings, queens and dolls one can take.

Great way to learn a new language for free or just spend downtime productively. I wish some of the stories came sooner for the Japanese course, and maybe a lite version of the talking with AI in the language you're learning existed in the free with ads option. The exercises where you listen to a conversation and pick out the topics being discussed are nice but I wish there were more of them to mix things up a bit more. Otherwise, an awesome app.

Constantly advertises Super/Max, that's fine. Constantly shows the monthly price for Super/Max, no problem. Want to get Super/Max, and they will charge you the annual fee. I imagine they hope people will forget to cancel the free trial or forget to cancel when the annual charge renews. I find it quite an exploitative approach to subscriptions.

The app does not allow for slower voice lessons - either superfast or super slow, neither of which are normal speaking speeds. No useful information for learning new words for new lessons, it just throws new words and sentences at you, which you will get wrong, which does not build confidence or an underatanding of what you are suppose to take from the lesson. If it weren't for the fact I already paid for a subscription and have other family members using it, I would have left.

I haven't been on Duolingo for so long but it's really good to learn a new language. I like that there's a language score that tells you how you would perform in the real world and it's pretty accurate for the most part. However, the app itself sometimes has performance issues that causes learners to lose progress in that lesson. Aside from the issues with the app hanging sometimes causing loss in progress I would generally recommend the app for learning a new language.

I love duolingo but I'm getting done with the ads, it was alright before, but they're getting more and more annoying... It's slowing down my progress and I'm honestly losing motivation because each time I complete a lesson I get like 2 or 3 ads. Isn't learning supposed to be free? wasn't this the app's purpose from the start? It doesn't look so free anymore.. Idk.

Since the new changes on Duolingo is has been a terrible experience! The algorithm of being in leagues is so messed up that no matter how many lessons you do, you are always put in the demotion zone. I have been using this app for years and this is the first time I am so annoyed at it. If this continues I will not be renewing my subscription ever again!! Very disappointed!

I enjoy this ap a lot, most of the time. I don't mind that you have to pay to get more hearts or that there are ads, that's to be expected with any free ap. But suddenly the ads don't have a close button no matter how long I wait. Nothing to do but quit the ap. And there goes the lesson - no credit, have to do it again, and no hearts refunded. This is a pretty awful bug :-(

Was great, mostly free language app, now too many ads, (some really long) they have eroded away key features unless you pay their subscription. It's no longer a level playing field. You can no longer practice to earn all the stars. When you are empty, you can get one star only. I've been on here for years, but I'm close to uninstalling it. Also, when you complete a lesson, you have to watch the ad, but also go through all the button stages or it doesn't count your score. Next day it

Overall a good app, but I had to wait for so long for a specific German story lesson, and it was so long that it might as well take forever. And also, some speaking practices won't get my pronunciations correctly despite it already being correct. But recently one issue is that some of the scores for my language courses are not appearing. Pls fix the issue, thanks.

I have been using Duolingo for 400+ days, always praising it to other people because it's a good way to learn some words/ease into a language. Some lessons are frustrating because the smallest autocorrect or spelling will register wrong when it's just like capatilisation (on a phone, mistakes happen) but nonetheless... I use it a lot. Now, my friends and I woke up to find out you can no longer do practise lessons to rewin one heart, meaning you cannot continue your streak without paying. This i

I have been very happily using the free app for years. Has anyone else noticed the recent change in advertising. I'm sure the ads are longer, and they only show super duolingo ads. I'm finding the marketing ploy too aggressive for my tastes and am probably going to delete the app. Especially now that there are othe language apps on par with it.

I used to be dedicated to this app. It taught me Spanish, it's helped me quickly learn enough of multiple languages to get about, and I have a 1600+ day streak. However, with this new ad heavy update, which means the user has now lost the ability to earn new hearts by doing a review lesson (now you can only get them for watching an ad) I'm getting frustrated with the app (as I know other users are) and am quickly falling out of love with it. I may even have to give up my multi year streak

Subscribed to German course about 4 weeks ago. Initially I enjoyed the gamiification, encouragement to learn, and animation. But the novelty has worn off. It has been teaching me the same simple set of words for the last 2 weeks and if I have to repeat them again I'm going to scream. In German even. Like a gambling machine, the app is rigged to force you spend more money to advance your learning even if you subscribe. Nicht beeindruckt (not impressed). Waste of a potentially great app.

Wow, how this app has changed. Not useful, advanced lessons only focus on a handful of words that repeat in the exact same sentences each week. The app's focus is on gimmicky animations, trying to stay relevant with kids, and trying to scam you into getting a paid subscription that doesn't actually add any value. This could be helpful for a short period of time if you just want something -- anything -- to jump start your language learning. But you're better off getting a specalised app.
