I'll give it 4 stars because it doesn't allow for you to save your streak, and there's been a few times where I've played and it just didn't register so I've lost my streak or had a "streak freeze" used. There have also been a few times where I did multiple lessons, and it didn't register, so I couldn't gain EXP or move on to the next lesson, which was frustrating. Other than that, I think it's great.

The competition style learning does have its benefits as it pushes you to stay on top of the leaderboard, but the fact that you're dependant on hearts pisses me off lmao. Love the streaks, but kinda lame that you could be spending 10 minutes trying to finish 1 three-minute-lesson bc you have to watch videos to get hearts. So keep in mind that this is still a game that, regardless of whether or not it helps you with learning a language, has a PTW system.

Good for learning some language like English and Japanese, but in Arabic lessons, I noticed there are fewer variations to the modules, and they even include local dialects such as egyptian to it. Also, recently there's a bug in Japanese that won't allow me to check my answer and proceed even when I have arranged the words correctly. Overall okay and helpful, but if you want to learn the languages seriously, take external courses and don't solely rely on Duolingo.

The last couple of updates are full of bugs. When I try to select a lesson, it shows 60 points, but after completing it, I only get 45. I activate boosters, but they don’t apply. In Math, when I try to match options, even if I pair them correctly, some still remain unselected. I complete a lesson, but it still warns me that I might lose my streak because Duolingo didn’t count it. The app is really buggy right now—what’s going on?

Good for learning vocabulary and introducing sentence structure, although some people have told me that Japanese people don't actually speak like that. The grammar is non-existent. You really need to have sources other than Duolingo on the side because there's no explanation in the app of Japanese grammar, which is pretty complicated. The listening exercises are inadequate as well. Lots of bugs and reporting them is to no avail. Keep your money for better apps.

It's fine, but the free version is just too tedious at this point. And there's no way to practice for hearts anymore? You can only watch ads for a heart now. I'm sick of Temu ads. The paid version removes them and you have unlimited hearts but like... the paid version ain't really worth the money. If I'm paying I'd rather pay for an actual course or program. Anyway yeah ads have ruined it completely and I'm uninstalling it. I'd only recommend this if you just want an easy start to learning.

Good. Expansive. The subscription is completely optional, since everything can be done without any issues without it, and even the ads themselves are not that interuptive, since they only appear at the end of a lesson. However, one detail that doesn't sit well with me is the price of starting a legendary lesson, which costs 100 diamons without the subscription. This is very annoying and makes doing legendary lessons basically impossible, or at least not worth it without the subscription.

Dear Duolingo Team, I just wanted to take a moment to express how much I absolutely love this app! I’ve recently started learning Korean, and it’s been such a fun and creative journey. The app makes learning feel effortless and enjoyable, and I find myself eagerly looking forward to each lesson. The design is intuitive, and the bite-sized lessons fit perfectly into my busy schedule, making it easy to stay on track. The gamified approach keeps me motivated, and I can see progress

I paid for duolingo plus because of the extra features. I paid for a full year. Now they have a higher level "dulingo super" and all the things I paid for are behind that pay wall. Don't waste your money on this app. They'll just make a third paywall later. I want my money back. What I bought doesn't exist. It was false advertising. If I could give zero stars, I would.

Overall the app can improve because they don't teach you the words and they expect you to know what it means. I find it very hard to try and learn a language if I have to guess to get the word to get it correct. The good things are that it improves every part of a language like speaking, listening and others. In the game I would rate the game 3/5 stars but there is definitely room for improvement.

it seems from my first time using the app for a different language a few years ago that there is more focus on actual things not weird phrases you would never use (may come later). I am finding way too many ads now, I don't even remember seeing any or if there was, it was much less. Makes learning, not fun to see ads that you can't skip, and it takes you out of the learning part of it, to then becoming just keeping your streak and not actually learning.

Professional linguists meet mediocre software engineers. The core functionality of this so is really good. I've pepped up my rusty Swedish and started to learn Italian at an unexpectedly high pace. Can recommend! Then why only 3 stars? The gamification part of language learning (where you get XP and badges for practicing and participate in tournaments) is full of bugs that didn't get resolved in months. Customer service is practically non-existent!

I am rating with this not because Duolingo isn't good - I actually find it very helpful. Going from a novice in Spanish to being able to converse with people feels very amazing. However , the ads are becoming too much. Two ads after each lesson is excessive, and its frustrating sometimes that I leave the app before finishing a lesson. You have done us a great help by making this app free, but pls reduce the ads. Thank you!

good for building vocabulary and getting used to grammar, but I wouldn't be able to learn chinese from scratch using duolingo alone. It works for me because I knew the basics and the leaderboards keep me hooked. The most efficient way to compete is the play morning and night each day, which is a good habit, but the rewards for the main lessons are not competitive xp/hr when lessons get trickier. If you want to focus on learning, you need to use methods that reward less xp.

I have used Duolingo for almost 3 years but it no longer provides me with the learning which I got at the beginning. The app has been tweaked so many times and now the free version is rubbish as many of the revision lessons are unavailable. The paid version (what Duolingo calls 'Super') is okay but you'll have to contend with not getting all your points, which kind of negates a game/points based learning platform.

Has quite a few glitches where you lose progress. This is quite annoying as it is a lot of effort to regain the progress, and as you've already done the lessons it is very boring and demoralising. Invasive ads you cannot escape becoming more frequent now. App is rapidly becoming more predatory and lower quality lessons with frequent errors. Was a good app several years ago

The lessons are an easy, helpful and educational way to learn Spanish. Just the right pace to understand and speak this beautiful language. The quests are great! They're challenging enough to get your brain thinking but not overwhelming. I actually look forward to my daily lessons! I'm 60 years old and my brain doesn't always retain the lessons. I find the best way to remember is to write down the words and sentences. So far, so good!

I play Duolingo multiple times a day every single day for the past 1640 days, and the recent update is really annoying. The app gets a threatening icon when the day is almost over, and by changing the icon, it rearranges my app, making me have to drag it back to its place every time. Not only that, recently a lot of shaming is going on to make people do their lessons. I will do it, I have been doing it for the past 1640 days, so I really don't need this. If anything, this demotivated me a lot.

I have a streak of over 650 days in Spanish. Duolingo has been great and fun. But the recent removal of "practice to earn hearts" is ridiculous. If you don't complete your lesson on your first attempt, you're forced to pay or watch ads just to keep your streak going. It makes it so much harder to get a quick lesson in on the go or before uni. For an app that puts such a focus on maintaining your streak, removing an option to keep learning to get your streak is unfair and greedy.

It's a fun easy way to learn a new language or brush up on your current one. Big complaint is the speech recognition in the app. It is TERRIBLE!!! I repeat a phrase and get it right, then I repeat the same phrase the same way and it marks all or half the words wrong. Then sometimes I say nothing correct and it marks it as perfect. This issue needs to be fixed ASAP, as it makes the speaking sections unplayable.

Too much advertising already, making everything just to buy the subscription, I was ok when there were adds to keep the learning free, now there are too much, and the lessons are made already just to keep you longer in the app, not to teach you things faster. Hundreds of lessons of just repeating the same things, just waste of time now. Once it was a very nice app teaching you a language fast. Now it's not anymore. I'm just deleting it.

Recently the advertising on Duolingo has been incredibly aggressive without a subscription. Some of the ads they push make it impossible to continue learning without restarting the app if you're unlucky to be come across them. Additionally they also have started to push their subscription service even more. I get a super ad after almost every completed lesson and/or exercise.

It definitely will get the job done for the most part and I enjoy the exercises. But when I tried it a few years ago, they had aoeaking exercises. Now I see threads of 100s of people who no longer have access to speaking, and they layouts don't look the same for everyone. They need to admit if there is an issue or if it's been removed. Speaking is kind of CRUCIAL when learning a new language.

App is inexplicably stuck in light mode and the setting to change it has been removed. Therefore it is now unusable because the bright background hurts my eyes. The option to change your daily goal in the app has also been removed. Have submitted two bug reports with no response. These were basic features and removing them makes absolutely no sense. Uninstalled, as the browser version now has better functionality, and no stupid incessant ads either.

Recently, there's been a few bugs. Choosing your quest partner glitches out (it pops up and then almost immediately just disappears) which is insanely infuriating. Also, I wish we could turn off the voice that repeats every word you click. It's extremely frustrating and distracting. The challenges where you pick the words to copy a sentence, you can't go back to change 1 word without having to undo everything up until that word. All quite annoying. But fix the friend quest thing.

27.02.25 I've stopped playing as the levels are few. Completed the last level 3 times. For me, there is no incentive to climb to the top! Anymore. It's such a shame. 27th October 24 Awfully at the moment keeps freezing. Having to stop my game yo get the app to work properly. S23. Come on, sort it out. The latest update is awful. Unable to type on some of the pages, it freezes. Why release when it's got such huge problems. I'm enjoying learning French. Still need to practice speaking.

Great app, but impossible to contact support when something goes wrong. I did a progress test for Japanese, and after passing it suddenly the entire course was autocompleted, even though I've only ever done section 1. Now I can't do any of the lessons that I actually need to progress my language study. No support function or way to contact anyone who can help. :(

Duolingo is a very popular language-learning app, and its ratings and reviews tend to be quite positive overall. Here's a breakdown of some key points to consider: * Strengths: * It's user-friendly and gamified, making language learning fun and accessible. * It offers a wide range of languages. * The basic version is free, which is a significant advantage. * It's effective for building foundational vocabulary and grammar skills. * It has expanded to include math and music courses

The teaching you give us is excellent but it's taking a lot of time. But we must say, maybe teaching and learning is a big progress. But one thing which is unacceptable in Duolingo is that even with our without super Duolingo there is no purpose in giving advertisement. That's not encouragable by everyone. We would really appreciate if you let us study with no distraction. We thought that the best teacher in the is Duolingo, teaching with no money, yes it is but with a lot of advertisements. Ty.

I do think the approach in which they try to teach languages is great and it did work for me to a certain point. BUT they're locking more and more features behind a paywall which makes it increasingly more frustrating to continue to learn. There's A LOT of ads, half of them just for giving them money so you can continue to learn. The app would be perfect if their main goal wouldn't just be to get you to spend money and if they'd lie a little less.

One complaint is that they do not provide European Portuguese. First lesson learning animal words such as armadillo or elephant, not essential! I think beginners would like to learn basics such as ordering food or finding out train times etc. That has yet to come up and I've been working on it for around five months. Although I appreciate that repetition is needed it's doesn't vary enough with the same key words cropping up time after time. Not worth paying for!

Used to be a decent language tool, but the more AI features they introduce, the more unusable it becomes. It keeps saying fully correct sentences contain typos, and the "speech" function seems to have stopped recognising speech about 50% of the time. Keeps re-teaching the same things over and over again, but never bothers to explain irregular verbs. A shame to see a decent resourced ruined by underreasearched and non-functioning AI.
